brief_summary:
Acute pyelonephritis (APN) is among the most common bacterial infections in older women. Oral step-down antibiotic therapy may potentially be associated with toxicity, particularly with fluoroquinolones or trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, espcially in geriatric patients. The emergence of resistant strains reduces the choice of oral step-down treatment, thereby increasing the risk of nosocomial complications related to intravenous access and prolonged hospitalization.

Fosfomycin trometamol (FT) has broad activity against Enterobacterales, including resistant strains. It has an excellent safety profile and moderate ecological impact, and has been used for several years to treat cystitis. Recent studies have demonstrated its efficacy as an oral step-down therapy for the treatment of E.coli APN in younger women. Its efficacy in a geriatric population remains to be demonstrated.

The primary objective is to demonstrate the non-inferiority, in terms of clinical cure, of FT compared with an alternative active antibiotic as step-down therapy for E. coli APN in older women.

FOSFOLD is a national, multicenter, randomised, comparative, phase 3, non-inferiority trial (1:1), open-label with two parallel treatment groups. After 3 or 4 days of appropriate empirical antibiotic therapy, women aged 75 or over with E.coli APN will be randomised to receive either 3g of FT once daily or an alternative antibiotic treatment in accordance with current french guidelines, for a total of 10 days.

The primary endpoint is clinical cure at Day 17, i.e. 10 days after completion of antibiotic therapy.

If non-inferiority of FT is confirmed, it could provide a new therapeutic approach for oral step-down therapy in the older patients with APN. Its favorable tolerability profile could help prevent common geriatric complications, such as delirium, falls and malnutrition. Ultimately, it could help prevent some of the iatrogenic functional decline associated with hospitalisation.
primary_outcomes: Clinical resolution
title: Fosfomycin Trometamol Compared With an Alternative Active Antibiotic as Step-down Therapy for the Treatment of Acute Pyelonephritis Due to Escherichia Coli in Elderly Women : a Randomized, Multicenter, Non-inferiority Trial

brief_summary:
Low back pain is a common complaint among postpartum females, often associated with diastasis recti abdominis (DRA), a condition characterized by the separation of the rectus abdominis muscles. This separation can lead to reduced core stability, altered biomechanics, and impaired functional performance. Effective rehabilitation strategies are essential to address pain, restore abdominal muscle integrity, and improve overall function in this population. This study aims to investigate the effects of Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS) with and without core stabilization exercises on low back pain, inter-recti distance (IRD), and transversus abdominis (TrA) thickness in postpartum females with diastasis recti abdominis. A randomized clinical trial will be conducted in which participants will be divided into two groups: one receiving TENS alone and the other receiving TENS combined with core stabilization exercises. Outcome measures will include pain intensity assessed through standardized scales, inter-recti distance measured using musculoskeletal ultrasound, and transversus abdominis thickness evaluated at rest and during contraction. These measures will be recorded before and after the intervention period to determine treatment effectiveness. Group A will receive TENS for pain relief.

Group B will receive TENS combined with core stabilization exercises such as abdominal drawing-in, pelvic tilts, and bridging for 4-6 weeks. Data will be analyzed using SPSS. Paired t-tests will assess within-group changes, and independent t-tests will compare between groups. A p-value ≤ 0.05 will be considered significant. The findings of this study are expected to provide evidence regarding the added benefit of core stabilization exercises when combined with TENS in postpartum rehabilitation.

This may help in developing more effective physiotherapy protocols for managing low back pain and abdominal muscle dysfunction in females with diastasis recti abdominis.
interventions: TENS combined with Core Stabilization Exercises
lead_sponsor: University of Management and Technology Lahore
primary_outcomes: DIGITAL VERNIER CALIPER
MSK ULTRASOUND
OSWESTRY DISABILITY INDEX
title: Effects of TENS With and Without Core Stabilization Exercises on Low Back Pain, Inter-Recti Distance, and Transversus Abdominis Thickness in Postpartum Women With Diastasis Recti Abdominis

brief_summary:
Background:

This protocol describes both a broader development initiative to address the needs of "zero-dose" (ZD) and under-vaccinated children, and embedded research. The embedded research includes primary data collection through interview and group discussions, and formal implementation research activities. All are funded by Gavi, the vaccine Alliance to generate timely information products for use in tailoring immunization strategies, and in tracking progress in reducing the numbers of ZD and under-vaccinated children.

Every year, nearly 10 million of the 72.5 million children that Gavi aims to reach in low-income countries do not receive a single dose of vaccine. Thus, these children are left susceptible to some of the world's deadliest diseases. The zero-dose (missing first dose of pentavalent vaccine) children account for nearly half of all vaccine-preventable deaths in Bangladesh. Approximately, 45% of the 9.7 million zero-dose (ZD) children reside in urban/peri-urban, remote rural or conflict settings of the country. Notably, about 16-20% of Bangladeshi population remain continuously unvaccinated or under-vaccinated which leaves critical gaps in protection and renders vulnerability to outbreaks.

Gavi and the Global Immunization Agenda 2030 have greatly intensified their emphasis on equity, intending to reach ZD, under-immunized (missing third dose of pentavalent vaccine) children and their communities. Gavi's new five-year strategy 5.0 to improve equity in vaccination coverage hinges on five key intervention areas within the Identify, Reach, Monitor, Measure, and Advocate (IRMMA) framework. To support this, Gavi is setting up "Gavi zero-dose country learning hubs" in order to identify and select a consortium of partners for implementing the learning hubs in Bangladesh, Mali, Nigeria and Uganda. The functioning of a country learning hub in each study country will ensure increased and timely availability of evidence to meet needs prioritized by country level stakeholders and that are aligned with Gavi learning priorities. Therefore, the ZD country learning hub in Bangladesh will conduct implementation research aligning Gavi's IRMMA framework for generating evidence-based interventions for reducing ZD and UI children. This will be accomplished by working in conjunction with the Government, local academic institutions and civil society organizations (CSOs) of the country.

Objectives:

The objectives of the research are to:

1. Understand the effective methods for identifying ZD children and missed communities
2. Identify the key barriers and enabling factors at different levels (policy down to community, and including supply, demand, and gender-related barriers) to identify ZD children
3. Develop and test appropriate approaches to reach ZD children and missed communities and to bring them into the health system in order to achieve full immunization
4. Identify the key barriers and enabling factors at each level (down to community) to reach ZD children and to bring them into the health system through full immunization

Methods:

This quasi-experimental pre-post design study will be conducted in six areas selected via rapid assessment that was conducted by Bangladesh country learning hub team. Each of the selected area will have a comparison area. The duration of the IR will be 18 months starting from September 2023. We will conduct the implementation research to test a set of interventions targeted to six types of areas already known to have higher levels of ZD. Mixed methods approach including baseline and endline household surveys and qualitative methods will be used for evaluation of effectiveness of the interventions. The baseline and endline survey data in the intervention and comparison areas will be analysed for comparison and estimation of difference-in-difference in ZD level. Multivariate analyses will be carried out to estimate the net effect of the intervention on zero-dose level, controlling for all confounders.

Outcome measures/variables:

The primary outcomes are the change(s) in prevalence of "ZD and under-immunized" children from baseline to endline periods.

primary_outcomes: Change in prevalence of "Zero-dose and under-immunized" children from baseline to endline
title: Implementation Research Zero-dose and Under-immunized Children

brief_summary: This is a pilot feasibility study to enable intensive outreach for marginalized patients with endometrial cancer (EC). Rural residents as well as patients who self-identify as Black or African American patients with EC have higher mortality rates. This study aims to introduce a treatment focused patient navigation intervention for marginalized patients with EC to address the multiple barriers these patients face. Patient navigation is a personalized program to help patients navigate the health care system and access medical and non-medical services. For example, patient navigators can provide services such as mediating/facilitating communication between patients and their providers/health care team, advocating for patient needs, identifying financial assistance and insurance-related resources, coordinating complex patient care, and providing patients with psychosocial support. This study will assess the implementation and effectiveness of a navigation intervention targeting multilevel barriers to care. The primary objective is to evaluate the fidelity of following the patient navigation intervention protocol.
primary_outcomes: Fidelity of the navigation intervention
title: Improving Rural Endometrial Cancer Care

brief_summary:
This is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm phase 2 study in adults with locally advanced (T3/T4) INI-1 (SMARCB1)-deficient sinonasal carcinoma, a very rare and aggressive cancer of the nasal cavity and sinuses. This cancer often invades the skull base, eyes, nerves, and surrounding critical structures, making surgery difficult and potentially disabling. Current standard treatment is usually surgery followed by radiotherapy, but complete removal is often difficult and recurrence is common. Standard chemotherapy before surgery has shown limited tumor shrinkage, so better pre-surgical treatment is urgently needed.

The purpose of this study is to find out whether giving an immunotherapy drug, finotonlimab, together with standard chemotherapy (paclitaxel plus cisplatin, the "TP" regimen) before surgery can shrink the tumor and improve treatment results. Finotonlimab is a PD-1 inhibitor that may help the immune system attack the cancer, and it is being given together with chemotherapy because the two treatments may work better in combination. All participants will receive 2 cycles of this combined treatment (each cycle is 21 days), followed by imaging tests to measure tumor response. If the tumor is considered removable, participants will then undergo surgery and, after recovery, standard postoperative radiotherapy.

The main question this study is trying to answer is: how many participants experience significant tumor shrinkage (objective response, defined as complete or partial response) after 2 cycles of neoadjuvant finotonlimab plus TP chemotherapy, as assessed by blinded independent imaging review using RECIST v1.1. The study will also look at safety, the rate of complete surgical removal (R0 resection), pathological response, disease-free and overall survival, quality of life, and whether important organs such as the eye can be preserved. About 20 participants will be enrolled across multiple centers. This study is expected to provide the first prospective evidence for this combination in this rare cancer and may help establish a new treatment option before surgery.
lead_sponsor: Eye & ENT Hospital of Fudan University
primary_outcomes: Objective Response Rate

Retrolaminar block (RLB)(a modified form of paravertebral block (PVB) and The ultrasound-guided rhomboid intercostal block (UG-RIB) used to alleviate the postoperative pain in video assisted thoracic surgery (VATS). We hypothesized that RLB may offer superior analgesic coverage and efficacy compared to The ultrasound-guided rhomboid intercostal block (UG-RIB) in the context of VATS.

1\. INTRODUCTION/ REVIEW (Maximum 1000 words) "References are needed" Thoracic surgery is specialized in the study of the chest organs and mainly refers to the lung, esophagus, and mediastinum diseases diagnosis and treatment, such as chest trauma, lung tumors, esophageal tumors, chronic obstructive emphysema, tuberculosis, esophageal functional diseases, diaphragmatic diseases, and congenital diseases of the chest. So many patients need to be treated with thoracic surgery in the world. Compared to thoracotomy, video-assisted thoracic surgery (VATS) has similar therapeutic effects with less invasion and relieves postoperative pain significantly, promoting rehabilitation \[1-3\].

However, the VATS still causes moderate to severe postoperative pain \[4, 5\]. Postoperative analgesia is a critical issue in accelerating the rehabilitation of patients during the perioperative period. The thoracic epidural block (TEB) is the gold standard for analgesia for thoracic surgery. However, the complications such as hypotension and nerve injury caused by it have been a problem that cannot be ignored.(6) RLB is a modified form of paravertebral block (PVB) \[7\]. While PVB is increasingly used for chest and abdominal surgeries due to its precise analgesic effects, it carries a risk of serious complications, including pneumothorax, hypotension, or nerve damage \[8,9\]. Even with ultrasound guidance, performing a traditional PVB remains technically challenging, with its success heavily reliant on the operator's expertise. RLB, as an improved alternative to PVB, has received growing attention in recent years. It involves the ultrasound-guided injection of local anesthetic between the lamina of the thoracic vertebra and the erector spinal muscle \[10\]. Compared to PVB, RLB is easier to perform, associated with fewer complications such as pneumothorax, intrathecal injection, or vascular damage. However, the spread of anesthetic in RLB appears highly variable and is dose-dependent \[11,12\].

The ultrasound-guided rhomboid intercostal block (UG-RIB) was discovered by Elsharkawy et al. in 2016 \[13\]. It has been reported that UG-RIB can ensure adequate analgesia in modified radical mastectomy and VATS \[14, 15\]. However, a comparison of the analgesic efficacy between RIB and retrolaminar (RLB)has yet to be reported. Therefore, it is urgent to compare the clinical effects of RIB and RLB in alleviating acute pain following video-assisted thoracic surgery to provide a scientific and practical theoretical foundation for selecting a subsequent analgesic strategy. It is of great significance to improve patients' life and rehabilitation and avoid other complications after the operation.

brief_summary:
This is a single-center, prospective, observational cohort study of patients with head and neck cancer (HNC) who receive intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT, including volumetric-modulated arc therapy, VMAT). HNC is the sixth most common cancer worldwide; in China, approximately 148,000 new cases and 78,000 deaths were reported in 2021. During and after radiotherapy, patients frequently develop severe acute toxicities-radiation-induced oral mucositis, orofacial pain, xerostomia, dysphagia, dehydration, and myelosuppression-that may lead to unplanned hospitalization or emergency department (ED) visits. Up to 28%-55% of HNC patients experience an ED visit or unplanned admission within 90 days of treatment, and rates may approach 58% in those receiving concurrent chemoradiotherapy. These events interrupt treatment, worsen prognosis, and impose a substantial burden on patients and the healthcare system.

Consecutive eligible patients will be enrolled before IMRT and followed from the first treatment fraction through 30 days after radiotherapy completion. At baseline, during radiotherapy, and before discharge, we will collect demographic and socioeconomic data; behavioral exposures (tobacco, alcohol, betel-nut use); comorbidity (Charlson Comorbidity Index, frailty); nutritional status (NRS-2002, BMI, weight loss); psychological screening; tumor- and treatment-related information; patient-reported symptoms (MDASI-HN); and serial blood tests from which inflammatory-nutritional indices (PNI, NLR, PLR, LMR, SII) are derived. The primary outcome is any unplanned hospitalization, including outpatient-to-inpatient transfer during treatment, ED-led admission, and post-treatment readmission; ED use is a key secondary outcome. We will estimate the incidence and reasons for these events, identify associated factors, characterize longitudinal symptom and laboratory trajectories, and develop and internally validate a risk prediction model (multivariable logistic regression, with a random forest model for comparison, presented as a nomogram). The model will support early identification of high-risk patients and targeted supportive interventions to reduce preventable acute-care utilization.

primary_outcomes: Incidence of Unplanned Hospitalization
title: Unplanned Hospitalization and Emergency Department Use in Patients With Head and Neck Cancer Receiving Radiotherapy

brief_summary:
Cortisol is a hormone that helps the body handle stress and maintain blood pressure. Doctors check if the adrenal glands (which make cortisol) are working correctly using a Synacthen test (SST). This test involves giving a drug that stimulates cortisol production and measuring how much is released.

For women taking oestrogen pills (found in birth control and hormone replacement therapy), the test results can be misleading. Oestrogen increases a substance in the blood called cortisol-binding globulin (CBG), which attaches to cortisol and makes some of it inactive. When doctors measure cortisol, they check both active and inactive forms. If CBG is high, the test can falsely suggest cortisol levels are normal, making it harder to tell if the adrenal glands are working correctly.

To avoid this problem, women taking oestrogen pills and gels/patches (transdermal) are asked to stop for 6 weeks before the test so that CBG/cortisol levels return to normal. However, this can cause uncomfortable symptoms like hot flushes, mood swings, and headaches.

Some women use transdermal oestrogen, which is absorbed through the skin instead. Unlike pills, there is some evidence that transdermal oestrogen doesn't affect CBG levels meaning women using them may not need to stop before an SST. This study will provide more evidence confirming that transdermal oestrogen is safe to continue before testing.

We will study three groups: women taking oestrogen pills, women using gel/patches, and women not taking oestrogen. By measuring CBG and cortisol every week, we aim to find out exactly when CBG returns to normal after stopping oestrogen pills. If it happens before 6 weeks, doctors may be able to shorten the break, making testing more manageable and more comfortable.

This research could improve testing for women taking oestrogen, potentially allowing those on gel/patches to continue treatment and those on pills to pause for a shorter time before testing.
lead_sponsor: Norfolk and Norwich University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
primary_outcomes: Changes in cortisol binding globulin (CBG) concentration and serum cortisol levels
title: Impact of Oral vs. Transdermal Oestrogen on Cortisol & CBG Before SST

brief_summary:
Sickle cell disease causes very painful episodes that can happen without warning. Pain is one of the biggest problems for people with SCD. Medicines like opioids can help, but they have serious side effects. Doctors are looking for other ways to treat pain.

Investigators have already found that music therapy - breathing exercises guided by a trained music therapist - can lower pain in adults with SCD. But investigators don't know exactly how it works yet inside the body.

This study will look at two possible reasons why music therapy helps:

* It may calm the body's "fight-or-flight" (sympathetic) nervous system, which can make pain worse when it is too active.
* It may boost the "calming" (parasympathetic) nervous system, which may ease pain and reduce inflammation.
* It may lower swelling and inflammation in the body, which also drives pain.

In residential care homes for the elderly, safeguarding the mental and emotional health of aged people is a key factor in their well-being and the quality of care they receive. Among these disorders, anxiety plays a central role. Furthermore, in aged people, anxiety is frequently associated with other psychological and functional vulnerabilities, notably depression and sleep disorders, with which it frequently interacts. Taken together, these factors contribute to a cycle of emotional, cognitive and functional vulnerability that can impair the well-being of residents in care homes. In light of these challenges, non-pharmacological interventions (NPIs), which have the potential to reduce anxiety and depression and improve sleep, represent a particularly promising complementary approach and are attracting growing interest in the care of aged people living in care homes. The Simone Veil Gerontology Institute and Care Home of Cannes Hospital wishes to offer its residents a sound immersion programme as part of their standard care. The audio content is sourced from the SOMEO Life digital platform, an audio-guided application accessible via wireless headphones connected to a tablet or smartphone, allowing for individual or group use. This application offers pre-recorded sessions on relaxation, guided breathing and sophrology tailored to aged people living in care homes. In this context, this study aims to explore and evaluate, within a pragmatic and institutional framework, the benefits of an audio-guided sound immersion programme (SOMEO Life platform) on the current levels of anxiety among residents living in care homes. Depressive symptoms, sleep disorders and the use of anti-anxiety medication will also be assessed.

An exploratory, prospective, single-centre, randomised, controlled, open-label study evaluating the benefits of a digital audio programme on anxiety in elderly people in care homes is implemented. Forty patients will be recruited (twenty per groups) and followed-up during 3 months.

Primary objective is to determine whether adding an audio-guided sound immersion programme to standard care reduces the current level of anxiety (state anxiety) in patients in residential care homes for the elderly. Study endpoint is State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI-Y), specifically the State Anxiety (Y-A) subscale.

brief_summary:
Background: Grade C trauma patients show no obvious severe injury at first assessment, but the mechanism or circumstances of the accident make serious lesions possible. Guidelines recommend a whole-body CT scan as first-line imaging1. The organization of the French trauma system varies between regions2. Île-de-France distinguishes level 1 trauma centers, which are authorized to manage the most severe patients, from level 2 hospitals, which can perform a full injury assessment3. Essonne has no level 1 trauma center, and most are located in Paris. Emergency dispatch physicians must therefore choose between performing the scan at the local hospital or transporting the patient directly to a trauma center. When a local scan is abnormal, specialist consultation, image transfer and secondary transport take time (median of about 6 hours4) and may worsen the prognosis.

Objective: To assess whether the proportion of abnormal whole-body CT scans in grade C trauma patients justifies systematic transport to a trauma center rather than local imaging.

Methods: Retrospective, multicenter cohort study of about 100 adult grade C trauma patients managed by an Essonne mobile emergency team (SMUR) in 2025 who underwent a whole-body CT scan. We will determine the proportion of abnormal scans, whether the lesions could be managed locally or required a level 1 or 2 trauma center, the secondary transfer rate, and the time to final destination.

Hypothesis: The proportion of abnormal scans, particularly those requiring specific medical care, is high enough to support performing the first whole-body CT scan at a trauma center.
interventions: Whole-body CT scan at the sector hospital
primary_outcomes: Proportion of pathological whole-body CT scans
title: Analysis of the Positivity Rate of Sector-based Whole-body CT Scans in Grade C Trauma Patients in Essonne

brief_summary:
This multicenter, open-label, randomized Phase III clinical trial evaluated the efficacy and safety of adding Polisorb® MP, an oral colloidal silicon dioxide adsorbent, to basic therapy in adults with mild to moderate atopic dermatitis.

The study included 161 patients in the efficacy analysis. Participants were randomly assigned to receive either basic therapy alone (81 patients) or basic therapy in combination with Polisorb® MP (80 patients). Basic therapy included skin care with emollients and pharmacological treatment, including cetirizine and topical pimecrolimus. The treatment period lasted 14 days, followed by an observation period. The primary endpoint was the change in the SCORAD index from baseline to Day 14. Itch intensity, dermatology-related quality of life, EASI and IGA scores were also assessed.

Both groups showed improvement in disease severity during treatment. The mean SCORAD score decreased by 21.5 points in patients receiving Polisorb® MP in addition to basic therapy, compared with 17.7 points in patients receiving basic therapy alone. The difference between the groups was statistically significant (p = 0.0028), favoring the addition of Polisorb® MP. Improvements in itch intensity and IGA scores also favored combination therapy, while differences between groups in EASI changes and changes in dermatology-related quality of life were not statistically significant.

A total of 34 adverse events were reported in 26 patients. No serious adverse events or deaths were reported. Gastrointestinal events, particularly constipation, were more frequent in the Polisorb® MP group. Other reported events included difficulty with defecation, abdominal discomfort, bloating, dry mouth and nausea. No new or unexpected safety concerns specific to Polisorb® MP were identified during the study.

The findings indicate that adding Polisorb® MP to basic therapy was associated with a greater reduction in SCORAD scores over 14 days than basic therapy alone. The results should be interpreted in the context of the open-label design and the short treatment period.
primary_outcomes: Change in Scoring Atopic Dermatitis (SCORAD) Index from Baseline to Day 14
title: Efficacy and Safety of Polisorb® MP in the Complex Therapy of Patients With Atopic Dermatitis

brief_summary:
Fertility problems are increasingly common in industrialized countries. It is estimated that 15-20% of couples of reproductive age have problems conceiving children naturally and the use of assisted reproductive treatment accounts for 1-3% of annual births. Among the causes of infertility, the female factor is responsible for approximately 40% of cases. The growing problem of infertility and the decline in the birth rate in Spain make absolutely necessary the improvement of assisted reproductive technology (ART). Actually, one of the main problems of ART is the election of the oocyte, as there is no method to select the best embryos for subsequent transfer. The average number of oocytes obtained from one woman in each cycle is 10-11, so the finding of a (some) biomarker(s) would have a great impact at a social and economic level and would commensurately reduce the economic cost of each cycle. Novel embryo assessment strategies are currently being developed and can be used alone or in combination with morphologic criteria. These include non-invasive methodologies as artificial intelligence using morphokinetic databases and the OMICS, like transcriptomic, proteomic and metabolomic. Among others, the transcriptome of the cumulus cells is a potentially valuable non-invasive biomarker. Indeed, it is already known that granulosa cells play a crucial role in the regulation of female fertility. The bi-directional communication between the oocyte and the surrounding cumulus cells is essential for the maturation of a developmentally competent oocyte, ovulation and fertilization, processes which are necessary for initiating and sustaining embryo development. Our work hypothesis is that the cumulus cell transcriptome would be directly related and give an essential information about oocyte maturation and fertilization ability.

Unfortunately, even though several studies on granulosa cell transcriptome analysis have been performed, the obtained data are still inconclusive. The main reason for this should be found in the study design which, in most cases, are performed in a small number of patients and presented a heterogeneous population.

Among others, there are great variations in the patients' age and physical characteristics, type of treatment, diagnosis, hormonal levels and endometrial receptivity. The main objective of this project is to find new unknown biomarker(s) of ongoing pregnancy by analyzing the whole transcriptome of the two granulosa cell layers surrounding the oocytes (cumulus cells and corona radiata). Specifically, the study aims to find a biomarker of oocyte maturity, of fertilization, of embryo quality, of euploid embryos, of pregnancy, early miscarriage or ongoing pregnancy, and finally, to find a correlation between these biomarkers and the morphokinetic of the embryos. An additional advantage of our project is the use of material that is obtained at the time of transvaginal ultrasound-guided oocyte retrieval but that is considered a waste and is usually discarded in Assisted Reproduction Centers. Therefore, the analysis of these cells does not suppose any change or bother for the women, in relation to the treatments of assisted reproduction.
primary_outcomes: Identify predicitve biomarkers for ongoing pregnancy
title: Differential Granulosa Cell Transcriptome Profiling as a Predictive Tool of Ongoing Pregnancy

brief_summary:
Over the last few years, a new approach using distal radial access had been employed for a various types of percutaneous interventions. The purpose was to further decrease the rate of vascular complications and proximal radial occlusion (RAO).

The feasibility of distal radial access in several specific groups of patients for conventional, complex coronary and non-coronary procedures was extensively studied and showed a variable rate of success between different operators, using different techniques. The main limitation is the rate of failure in cannulation that is related to the smaller diameter of the distal radial artery and the anatomic variability at the level of access site puncture. One of the solutions advocated by Hadjivassiliou et al. is the use of ultrasound-guided distal transradial acces (dTR)A, which is expected to reduce failure and complication rates.

A recent monocentric, single operator pilot study indicated a lower failure rate with ultrasound than conventional dTRA, without significant differences in puncture time and complication rate between the two approaches.

A specific ultrasound algorithm for distal radial puncture was recently developed and is currently used in our clinical daily practice, showing a 100% rate of success, in a selected group of patients that had favorable anatomic features. Imaging the distal radial artery by ultrasound could potentially be safer, select the proper candidates for this technique and increase the rate of successful cannulation. However, to date, the comparison of feasibility and safety between ultrasound-guided and conventional dTRA has not been reported.

The SOUND Distal trial is a pilot study measuring the reproducibility, rate of success, rate of complications and quality puncture measures.

The primary outcome is comparing the rate of success of dTRA cannulation between conventional and echo guided puncture. Secondary outcomes include quality puncture measures differences between the two approaches regarding patient scale pain/puncture time and number of attempts.

Other secondary end points include technic reproducibility among operators and the total rate of complications for both approaches.
primary_outcomes: first-wiring pass success rate
title: Conventional or Ultrasound Guided Puncture Technique for the Distal Radial Artery, Direct Comparison Study (Sound Distal Trial).

The education program targets employers (administrators) of United States (U.S.)-based emergency medical services (EMS) and fire department operations. primary_outcomes: Change in policy (EMS Administrators)
Change in sleep quality (Frontline EMS personnel)
title: The Sleep Health and Fatigue Education Program for the Administrators of Emergency Medical Services Agencies

brief_summary: This single-group, mixed-methods study explored changes following a 13-week group psychodrama programme in adults with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (MS). Participants were recruited from the demyelinating diseases unit of Mersin University Hospital, Türkiye, and attended weekly sessions of approximately 180 minutes in addition to their standard medical treatment. Loneliness, fatigue, cognitive performance, depressive and anxiety symptoms, and sleep quality were assessed at baseline, after the intervention and at 6-month follow-up. Individual semi-structured interviews conducted after the intervention and at follow-up explored participants' experiences of physical, cognitive, psychological and social change. Quantitative and qualitative findings were integrated within a convergent mixed-methods design.
primary_outcomes: Change in loneliness
title: Psychodrama for Adults With Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis: A Mixed-Methods Study

brief_summary: This is a multicenter, randomized, open-label, parallel-controlled Phase Ib clinical trial. It aims to evaluate the safety and preliminary efficacy of ACT201 Injection combined with standard therapy (PegIFNα, NA) in participants with chronic hepatitis B who are receiving NA treatment. A total of 40 participants with chronic hepatitis B will be enrolled. Eligible participants should have stable NA treatment, HBV DNA \< 100 IU/mL, negative HBeAg, and HBsAg ≤ 100 IU/mL. They will be randomized into four treatment groups at a 1:1:1:1 ratio.
primary_outcomes: Safety: number of participants with adverse event (AE), serious adverse events (SAE) and clinically significant examination results. Assessments include vital signs, physical examinations, laboratory tests, and 12-lead electrocardiograms (ECGs).
title: ACT201 Injection in Participants With Chronic Hepatitis B (CHB) on Nucleos(t)Ide Analog Therapy - Phase Ib

brief_summary: PRECAREX is a pilot randomized clinical trial with a two-arm parallel design aimed at evaluating the feasibility and safety of a preoperative weight loss intervention combining supervised exercise and calorie restriction in patients undergoing colorectal cancer surgery. The trial will also explore whether this intervention may improve surgical outcomes compared with usual care.
primary_outcomes: Feasibility of the preoperative intervention
Safety of the preoperative intervention
title: Preoperative Calorie Restriction and Exercise in Patients With Obesity Undergoing Colorectal Cancer Resection

brief_summary:
Restoration of arterial patency following recanalization of non-acute atherosclerotic middle cerebral artery (MCA) occlusion may improve cerebral blood supply. However, the extent to which restored perfusion is accompanied by changes in cerebral metabolism and functional brain network organization remains incompletely understood.

This prospective observational study, RESTORE, aims to characterize cerebral perfusion-metabolism recoupling and functional network recovery in patients with non-acute atherosclerotic MCA occlusion who undergo clinically indicated recanalization.

Integrated positron emission tomography/magnetic resonance imaging (PET/MR) will be used to assess cerebral perfusion, metabolic activity, and brain functional connectivity at protocol-defined time points. Imaging measurements will be evaluated in relation to vascular characteristics, recanalization status, and neurological and cognitive outcomes, as applicable.

The study seeks to clarify the temporal and spatial relationships among reperfusion, metabolic changes, and functional network reorganization, and to explore imaging markers associated with clinical recovery after recanalization.

The decision to perform recanalization and the selection of treatment strategies will be based on routine clinical care and will not be assigned by the observational study protocol.
primary_outcomes: Change in Perfusion-Metabolism Abnormality Burden in the Affected Hemisphere From Baseline to 1 Month After Recanalization (ΔPMB)
title: Integrated PET/MR Assessment of Brain Recovery After Recanalization of Non-Acute Atherosclerotic MCA Occlusion

brief_summary: This study aimed to evaluate the possible immunomodulatory effect of Azithromycin as an adjuvant treatment on the clinical and laboratory outcomes of children with newly diagnosed ITP through its effect on T-reg cells.
primary_outcomes: Change in Platelet Count
title: Azithromycin as an Adjunct to Corticosteroids in Children With Newly Diagnosed Immune Thrombocytopenia

brief_summary: This is a Phase II, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial of multiple subcutaneous administrations of GR2301 Injection to evaluate the efficacy, safety, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics in trial participants with vitiligo. Eligible trial participants will be randomized using stratified block randomization, with competitive enrollment across sites; they will be assigned to the experimental group or the control group in the order of successful screening.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of trial participants achieving F-VASI50 at the Week 24 (W24) visit.
title: A Clinical Trial of Multiple Doses of GR2301 Injection in Participants With Vitiligo.

brief_summary: Lumbar disc herniation can cause leg pain, difficulty with daily activities, and symptoms of depression or anxiety. This completed study compared disability and psychological symptom scores in patients who chose an image-guided injection with those who continued conservative care. Sixty-four patients at Tiemenguan People's Hospital were included in the analytical cohort, with 32 in each group. Treatment was chosen through patient preference and discussion with clinicians. Disability, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms were assessed before treatment and at a nominal three-month follow-up. Pain was recorded before and immediately after the first treatment session. The study examined whether the two treatment groups had different three-month scores. The comparison is observational and cannot establish that treatment caused the differences. This record is prepared after data collection; outcome ordering was determined after data collection.
interventions: Fluoroscopy-guided periradicular/epidural injection with reverse geometric planning
primary_outcomes: Oswestry Disability Index score at 3 months
title: Disability and Psychological Symptoms After Injection or Conservative Care for Lumbar Disc Herniation

brief_summary:
This proposal seeks to determine if the addition of Suzetrigine, a novel non-opioid pain medication, to a standardized multimodal pain management pathway significantly reduces total postoperative opioid consumption (measured in Morphine Milligram Equivalents \[MME\]) and improves patient-reported pain scores during the first 14 days following primary total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Prior to conducting a definitive randomized control trial (RCT), we propose a pilot study to inform the trial's design and feasibility.

Objective: To inform the design and feasibility of a definitive RCT comparing postoperative pain control with and without Suzetrigine after TKA. To achieve this objective, we will conduct a pilot trial and address the following aims:

1\) to determine if participant enrollment is feasible, 2) to assess compliance with treatment protocol and key aspects of the protocol, and 3) to refine data collection methods.
primary_outcomes: Participant enrollment
Protocol adherence
Data collection
title: A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial of Suzetrigine as an Adjunct to Multimodal Analgesia Following Total Knee Arthroplasty

brief_summary:
This is a Phase 3, multi-center, multi-national, randomized, open-label, active-comparator study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of venglustat in pediatric (age ≥2 years to ≤11 years) participants with GD3 who have been treated with ERT for at least 2 years, and have met therapeutic goals. Study details include: Study duration: a 52-week primary analysis period and a 52-week extended treatment period.

Treatment frequency:

* Daily tablets for venglustat for participants randomized to venglustat arm during primary analysis period and for all patients during extended treatment period.
* Cerezyme infusion every 2 weeks for participants randomized to Cerezyme arm during primary analysis period and, if needed, as rescue medication for participants in venglustat treated arm during primary analysis period or for any participant during extended treatment period.

Visit frequency: every 12 to 14 weeks during primary treatment period and 12-26 weeks during extended treatment period.
primary_outcomes: Percent change from baseline in magnetic resonance imaging(MRI) spleen volume (in multiples of normal [MN]) at Week 52
title: The Efficacy and Safety of Venglustat Compared With Cerezyme in Pediatric Participants 2 to 11 Years of Age With Gaucher Disease Type 3 (GD3)

brief_summary: GLP-1 receptor agonists delay gastric emptying and are associated with a higher rate of retained gastric content (RGC) during upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, even under standard fasting. No randomized trial has compared fasting strategies in this population. CLEAR-GLP1 is a multicentre, international, investigator-blinded randomized trial comparing a 24-hour clear liquid diet (followed by a 2-hour fast) with standard fasting (6 hours for solids, 2 hours for clear liquids) in adults on GLP-1 RA therapy undergoing elective upper endoscopy. GLP-1 RA therapy is not interrupted in either arm. The primary outcome is the rate of clinically significant RGC, defined as a GRACE stomach score of 0.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Retained Gastric Content
title: 24-hour Clear Liquid Diet vs. Standard Fasting for Upper Gastrointestinal Endoscopy in Patients Taking Agonists of the GLP-1 Receptor

brief_summary: This clinical trial will evaluate the safety, and effectiveness of ceftobiprole compared to standard-of-care antibiotic treatment in children from birth to less than 18 years of age with Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infection, including right-sided infective endocarditis (IE). The trial will also evaluate the pharmacokinetics of ceftobiprole.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants with Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events (TEAEs)
Percentage of participants with serious adverse events (SAEs)
Percentage of participants with treatment-related adverse events (AEs)
Percentage of participants with adverse events of special interest (AESIs)
Percentage of participants with adverse events (AEs) leading to discontinuation of study-drug treatment
Percentage of participants with treatment-emergent abnormal hematology laboratory test results
Percentage of participants with treatment-emergent abnormal blood chemistry laboratory test results
Percentage of participants with treatment-emergent abnormal urinalysis test results
Change from baseline in body temperature
Change from baseline in systolic blood pressure
Change from baseline in diastolic blood pressure
Change from baseline in respiratory rate
Change from baseline in heart rate
title: A Study of Ceftobiprole Compared With Standard Antibiotic Treatment in Children With Staphylococcus Aureus Bacteremia (SAB) Infection, Including Right-sided Heart Infection

brief_summary:
People with advanced liver disease often experience complex physical symptoms, emotional concerns, and practical difficulties, especially as their illness progresses. Currently, there are no questionnaires designed specifically to capture these needs and experiences. A purposely designed questionnaire could help healthcare professionals better understand patients' needs and improve the care they receive. The questionnaire must be tested to make sure that it is reliable, accurate and acceptable to patients. This process is known as validation.

This study is testing a new questionnaire called the Integrated Palliative care Outcome Scale- Liver (IPOS-Liver). It asks about symptoms and concerns experienced by people living with advanced liver disease.

The study will take place in two NHS hospitals in England. 71 NHS patients with advanced chronic liver disease will take part, together with healthcare professionals involved in their care. Patients and healthcare professionals will be asked to complete the IPOS-Liver questionnaire alongside other established questionnaires. These will be completed at two time points a few days apart. The results will be statistically analysed to see whether the new questionnaire gives consistent and useful results. A small number of patients will additionally be invited to take part in a 30-minute interview about their experience of completing the IPOS-Liver. Adult NHS patients in England will be invited to take part after the clinician caring for them identifies that they are eligible for the study.
primary_outcomes: Construct Validity
title: IPOS-Liver Validation Study

brief_summary: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is a highly aggressive neuroendocrine malignancy. Approximately 70% of patients are diagnosed with extensive-stage disease, and only a subset of patients benefit from immunotherapy. Under the leadership of Academician Sun Yan, the principal investigator, our research group previously relied on the Big Data Platform of the National Cancer Center and undertook major projects including those from the National Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine, the Beijing Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine for collaborative of major and difficult diseases with integrated traditional Chinese and Western medicine, as well as the National Key R\&D Program. A randomized controlled trial (RCT) of 600 cases demonstrated that the traditional Chinese medicine "Fuzheng Jiedu Huayu" (strengthening vital energy, detoxifying, and resolving stasis) combined with chemotherapy and immunotherapy synergistically improved progression-free survival and disease control rate in patients with extensive-stage SCLC. Building on this foundation, the current project will enroll 224 patients with extensive-stage SCLC (1:1 ratio). On the basis of first-line treatment with immunotherapy plus platinum-based agents and etoposide, patients will be administered either "Fuzheng Jiedu Huayu" traditional Chinese medicine or a placebo. The study will employ objective response rate, progression-free survival, and overall survival as outcome measures, conducting a multicenter, large-sample RCT. Additionally, a multimodal database of no less than 1000 cases will be established, striving to obtain an IND approval, thereby contributing to the realization of the goal set forth in the "Healthy China 2030" Planning Outline: "By 2030, increase the overall 5-year cancer survival rate by 15%."
primary_outcomes: Objective Response Rate, ORR
title: Clinical Study on Fuzheng Jiedu Huayu Therapy in Combination With Chemotherapy and Immunotherapy for Improving Survival Rates in Extensive-Stage Small Cell Lung Cancer

brief_summary: Patients with Parkinson's disease experience progressive deconditioning of the respiratory muscles, leading to weakness and potential ventilatory impairments. Evidence indicates that physical exercise positively affects these muscles in people with various clinical conditions. This study will evaluate the effects of multicomponent and resistance training on respiratory parameters and physical and functional capacities in individuals with Parkinson's disease. A total of 40 patients will be randomly allocated to two groups: 20 individuals in the multicomponent training group and 20 in the resistance training group. Both groups will undergo a three-month intervention with two sessions per week. All participants must continue standard pharmacological treatment for Parkinson's disease. Respiratory parameters will be assessed using respiratory pressure measurement and spirometry. Physical and functional capacities will be assessed using the Rikli and Jones test battery.
primary_outcomes: Inspiratory pressure
Forced Vital Capacity
title: Training in Adults With Parkinson's Disease

brief_summary: The aim of the study is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of oral ecnoglutide tablets in Chinese participants with overweight or obesity
primary_outcomes: Percentage Change in Body Weight
title: A Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of Ecnoglutide Tablets in Chinese Participants With Overweight or Obesity

brief_summary: This pilot randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate whether sending maternal health information via voice-based WhatsApp messages is more effective than text-based WhatsApp messages. The study enrolled 79 pregnant and breastfeeding women in Abuja, Nigeria, who were assigned to receive weekly voice messages, text messages, or standard care over an eight-week period. The primary goal is to determine if voice messaging produces greater improvements in maternal health knowledge and attitudes, which could offer a scalable, low-literacy-friendly tool to improve maternal health outcomes in Nigeria.
interventions: Participants received weekly maternal health audio messages delivered over eight weeks via a WhatsApp broadcast list. Message content was adapted from WHO and UNICEF maternal health education material
primary_outcomes: Maternal Health Knowledge Score (Scale b2)
title: Voice-Based vs. Text-Based WhatsApp Messaging for Maternal Health Knowledge and Attitudes Among Pregnant and Breastfeeding Women in Abuja, Nigeria

brief_summary: A 13-week longitudinal experimental study designed to determine how the level of neuromuscular fatigue induced by strength training influences chronic adaptations. Four assessment periods (pre-protocol, mid-point 1, mid-point 2, and post-protocol) will be used to measure neuromuscular, physiological, and structural parameters. A reference group will be included to assess measurement variability across the evaluation phases (this group will only undergo these assessments), while an experimental group will follow a standardized training protocol (in addition to the assessment phases).
primary_outcomes: maximal isometric strength
title: Influence of Neuromuscular Fatigue Accumulated During Training on Subsequent Chronic Adaptations: PROTECT-10

brief_summary:
Thyroid nodules are common clinical findings, and accurate differentiation between benign and malignant nodules is essential for appropriate patient management. Ultrasonography is the primary imaging modality for thyroid nodule evaluation, while the American College of Radiology Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System (ACR TI-RADS) provides a standardized approach for malignancy risk assessment.

Fine Needle Aspiration Cytology (FNAC) is an important diagnostic procedure for evaluating thyroid nodules, with cytological results classified according to the Bethesda System.

This prospective study aims to evaluate and compare the diagnostic accuracy of FNAC and ACR TI-RADS 3 classification in the assessment of thyroid nodules.

The study will include 30 adult patients with TI-RADS 3 thyroid nodules at Sohag University Hospital. All participants will undergo clinical examination, thyroid ultrasonography, TI-RADS classification, and ultrasound-guided FNAC. Cytological findings will be reported according to the Bethesda System. Histopathological examination of surgically excised thyroid specimens will be performed whenever available.

The diagnostic performance will be assessed using sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value. Statistical analysis will be performed using SPSS.
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic Performance of Fine Needle Aspiration Cytology (FNAC) Compared with Histopathological Findings in ACR TI-RADS 3 Thyroid Nodules
title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Fine Needle Aspiration Cytology (FNAC) Compared to TI-RADS 3 in the Evaluation of Thyroid Nodules: A Prospective Study

brief_summary: The purpose of this pilot study is to establish the feasibility of home-based Auricular Vagal Neuromodulation Therapy (AVNT™) in Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) patients, generate preliminary efficacy data on autonomic function outcomes, and explore whether timing variation influences treatment response.
conditions: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) Stages G3 to G5
primary_outcomes: Change in Orthostatic Heart Rate Response
title: Transcutaneous Auricular Vagal Neuromodulation Therapy (AVNT™) in Chronic Kidney Disease Autonomic Dysfunction

brief_summary:
Vitiligo is a chronic skin disorder for which new therapeutic options, including topical and oral Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors, are emerging. In this evolving therapeutic context, long-term follow-up of patients and documentation of their treatment history are important to better understand treatment outcomes and safety in routine clinical practice.

This study is a French multicenter pilot cohort conducted as a preliminary step toward the development of a national vitiligo registry. It aims to document the clinical course of patients with vitiligo, their treatments and treatment outcomes, and adverse events occurring during treatment. The study will also collect clinical, quality-of-life and patient-reported outcome data and explore potential factors associated with treatment failure or the occurrence of adverse events.
interventions: Vitiligo treatments in routine clinical practice
primary_outcomes: Clinical course of vitiligo under treatment assessed by T-VASI
Clinical course of vitiligo under treatment assessed by sIGA
title: VItiligo RegisTry adUlts And chiLdren-France

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial aims to investigate the effects of Thai food-specific inhibition control training on psychological, physiological, behavioral, and neurophysiological outcomes in Thai adults with obesity.

A total of 72 participants will be randomly assigned to either a Thai food-specific inhibition control training group (n = 36) or a general inhibition control training group (n = 36). Both groups will receive training five days per week for eight consecutive weeks.

Psychological, anthropometric, and eating-related behavioral outcomes will be assessed at baseline (T0), immediately after the eight-week intervention (T1), and at a four-week post-intervention follow-up (T2). Event-related potential components, including N2 and P3, will be assessed at baseline and immediately after the intervention.

The study will compare changes in outcomes between the two intervention groups over time to determine whether Thai food-specific inhibition control training produces different effects from general inhibition control training.
primary_outcomes: Change in Body Weight
Change in Body Mass Index
Change in Waist Circumference
title: Effects of Thai Food-Specific Inhibition Control Training on Psychophysiological Outcomes in Thai Adults With Obesity

brief_summary:
Difficulty with bowel movements is one of the most serious side effects of spinal cord injury and one that most severely restricts everyday life. Many people affected take 30 to 60 minutes, or considerably longer, to pass stools. This is accompanied by a significantly slowed bowel transit, which often leads to a feeling of fullness, flatulence and chronic pain. The study investigates a method suitable for everyday use to support bowel function: electrical stimulation of the abdominal muscles. This involves applying adhesive electrodes to the abdomen and controlling them via a small device. The treatment is carried out independently at home - 30 minutes before each planned bowel movement. Two stimulation settings are being compared: i) Motor stimulation: The current strength causes a noticeable contraction of the abdominal muscles. ii) Sensory stimulation: The intensity is lower and is perceived merely as a gentle tingling sensation. The procedure is divided into several phases. Before stimulation begins, baseline values are recorded during a two-week pre-observation phase. Subsequently, both stimulation methods are applied one after the other for 12 weeks each, interspersed with a six-week break without stimulation. Which participant starts with which type of stimulation is determined at random. A final six-week follow-up phase assesses whether any improvements achieved persist after the end of treatment.

During the study, participants will keep a diary and, together with specialists, complete two questionnaires. Bowel transit time will be measured in a simple and safe manner (using maize grains and a capsule containing blue food colouring). In addition, stool samples will be collected at five specified time points to analyse changes in the gut microbiota. The aim is to evaluate a gentle, practical method that facilitates the bowel movement process, promotes gut health and noticeably improves the quality of life of people with spinal cord injury.
primary_outcomes: Defecation time
Defecation Time (Minutes)
title: Abdominal Neuromuscular Electrical Stimulation to Treat Neurogenic Bowel Dysfunction in Chronic SCI

brief_summary: This first-in-human study will evaluate the safety and tolerability of phelimin, an investigational oral treatment being developed for people with phenylketonuria (PKU). Phelimin is designed to bind the amino acid phenylalanine in the gut, which may reduce its absorption from food and support its removal from the body in stool. The study will include healthy volunteers and adults with classical PKU. Participants will receive single doses of phelimin at increasing dose levels and will undergo safety assessments, including monitoring for side effects, laboratory tests, and gastrointestinal symptoms. The study will also explore whether phelimin affects blood phenylalanine levels after a standardised protein challenge.
primary_outcomes: Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events
AEs
Serious adverse events (SAE)
title: A First-in-Human Study of Phelimin in Healthy Volunteers and Adults With PKU

brief_summary: This retrospective cohort study evaluated whether the timing of epidural analgesia initiation affects labor outcomes in obstetric patients. Patients were categorized as EARLY (cervical dilation less than 4 cm, n=59) or LATE (4 cm or greater, n=129) at epidural placement. The primary outcome was second stage labor duration in vaginally delivering patients (n=177). Secondary outcomes included first stage duration, epidural-to-delivery interval, total fentanyl consumption, cesarean section rate, and neonatal outcomes. EARLY epidural initiation was associated with significantly longer second stage duration (37 vs 25 min, p=0.003), higher fentanyl consumption (56 vs 36 mcg, p\<0.001), and higher cesarean section rate (13.6% vs 2.3%, p=0.005). Neonatal outcomes were comparable between groups.
conditions: Labor Pain and to Reduce Pain
primary_outcomes: Second Stage Labor Duration
title: Effect of Epidural Analgesia Timing on Labor Duration and Obstetric Outcomes

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to learn whether simulation training with an ambient artificial-intelligence (AI) coach improves how physicians lead trauma resuscitations. The main question it aims to answer is:

\- After coach-assisted training, do participants lead simulated trauma resuscitations without the coach better than they did before training?

Researchers will compare each participant's performance on cases led without the coach before and after training.

Participants will:

* Lead simulated trauma resuscitations by voice in a trauma-bay simulator
* Lead cases without the coach, then training cases with the coach, then further cases without the coach
* Complete short surveys

Blinded attending physicians score each case from a recording.
primary_outcomes: Change in Unassisted Team-Leader Performance Score From Baseline to Post-Training
title: Training Trauma Team Leaders With an Ambient AI Coach in Simulated Resuscitations

brief_summary:
People with a slow heart rhythm may need a permanent pacemaker. Conventional pacemakers use a device placed under the skin and wires that pass through veins into the heart. Leadless pacemakers are placed directly inside the heart without a chest pocket or these wires. Both approaches can provide pacing, but their effects on heart function and heart-failure-related problems need to be compared.

LEAP-HF will compare an indication-adapted leadless pacemaker strategy with a conventional transvenous pacemaker strategy in 760 adults for whom either approach is clinically appropriate. Participants must have a left ventricular ejection fraction above 40% and must not require a defibrillator, cardiac resynchronization therapy, or chronic atrial pacing. Participants will be assigned by chance, in equal proportions, to the two strategies. The device and pacing mode will be selected according to the participant's clinical indication within the assigned strategy.

The main question is whether the leadless strategy is not unacceptably worse than the conventional strategy for pacing-induced cardiac dysfunction during 12 months of follow-up. This outcome includes a qualifying deterioration in heart pumping function, pacemaker syndrome, heart failure requiring hospitalization, or an upgrade to cardiac resynchronization therapy. The prespecified non-inferiority margin is an absolute difference of 7 percentage points.

Assessments include heart ultrasound, pacemaker checks, an electrocardiogram, a blood test for NT-proBNP, symptom assessment, and questionnaires about health and quality of life. There will be a telephone contact at 6 weeks and in-person visits at 6 and 12 months after implantation. The study will also compare heart function, complications, further procedures, and deaths. Participants and treating teams will know which pacing system was implanted; selected clinical events will be reviewed by an independent committee unaware of the assigned treatment.
lead_sponsor: Karl Landsteiner University of Health Sciences
primary_outcomes: Cumulative incidence of pacing-induced cardiac dysfunction
title: Leadless Versus Conventional Pacemakers: Effects on Heart Function and Heart Failure

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of adding AneuFix Injectable Polymer sac filling to standard endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) in patients with an infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) who are at high risk of developing a Type II endoleak after EVAR. The study will include adult men and women who are candidates for elective EVAR and meet predefined imaging criteria indicating a high risk of post-procedural Type II endoleak.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the addition of AneuFix Injectable Polymer to standard EVAR reduce the occurrence of Type II endoleaks, prevent aneurysm sac growth, and reduce the need for AAA-related reinterventions within 12 months after treatment?
* Is treatment with AneuFix Injectable Polymer safe, as measured by the rate of major adverse events within 30 days after the procedure?

Researchers will compare EVAR plus AneuFix Injectable Polymer sac filling with standard EVAR alone to determine whether sac filling improves aneurysm-related outcomes and reduces complications associated with persistent blood flow into the aneurysm sac following EVAR.

Participants will:

* Undergo screening assessments, including review of medical history, imaging studies, and eligibility criteria.
* Be randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive either:
* Standard EVAR with AneuFix Injectable Polymer sac filling, or
* Standard EVAR alone.
* Attend follow-up visits at approximately 1 month, 6 months, 1 year, 2 years, 3 years, 4 years, and 5 years after treatment.
* Undergo imaging assessments, including CT angiography and ultrasound or magnetic resonance angiography, to evaluate the presence of endoleaks, aneurysm sac size, and other aneurysm-related outcomes.
* Be monitored for adverse events, reinterventions, aneurysm-related complications, and survival throughout the 5-year follow-up period.
* Complete quality-of-life questionnaires at selected study visits.

This multicenter, randomized, controlled study plans to enroll approximately 150 participants at sites across Europe and follow them for up to 5 years after treatment.
primary_outcomes: Composite Treatment Success at 12 Months
Major Adverse Event (MAE) rate within the 30-day follow-up period after the procedure
title: Safety and Effectiveness Assessment of AneuFix Injectable Polymer Sac Filling to Assure Long-term Durability of EVAR.

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate the effects of the Peachbiotic supplement on gut health in adults experiencing gastrointestinal symptoms. The trial is a single-arm, open-label, virtual study in which all 40 enrolled participants will use the test product daily for 12 weeks.

Participants will take one capsule of the product once daily in the morning with food and will complete self-reported questionnaires at Baseline, Week 4, Week 8, and Week 12 to assess changes in gut health outcomes including bloating, digestive comfort, regularity of bowel movements, gasiness, and general well-being.
primary_outcomes: Change in Gut Health (GSRS)
Change in Gut Health (Bristol Stool Scale)
title: A Clinical Trial to Evaluate the Effects of a Supplement on Gut Health

brief_summary:
This prospective, randomized, controlled clinical trial aims to evaluate the efficacy of ultrasound-guided thoracolumbar fascia (TLF) injection as an adjunct to standard conservative treatment in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic nonspecific low back pain.

A total of 60 patients aged 18-65 years, diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus for at least one year and experiencing chronic nonspecific low back pain for at least three months, will be enrolled. Eligible participants will be randomly assigned to two groups. The intervention group will receive ultrasound-guided thoracolumbar fascia injection in addition to standard conservative treatment, while the control group will receive standard conservative treatment alone, consisting of patient education and a structured exercise program.

Clinical assessments will be performed at baseline and at 1 and 3 months after treatment. Treatment outcomes will include pain intensity measured using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS), functional disability assessed using the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), pressure pain threshold (PPT) measured by algometry, and analgesic consumption.

Thoracolumbar fascia thickness will be measured using ultrasonography at baseline to investigate its potential association with treatment response. Diabetes-related characteristics, including HbA1c levels, diabetes duration, and peripheral neuropathy status, will also be recorded.

The primary objective is to determine whether adding ultrasound-guided thoracolumbar fascia injection to standard conservative treatment provides greater improvement in pain intensity and functional disability compared with standard conservative treatment alone. The study will also explore whether baseline thoracolumbar fascia thickness and diabetes-related characteristics are associated with clinical outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Change in Low Back Pain Intensity Measured by the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS)
title: Ultrasound-Guided Thoracolumbar Fascia Injection for Chronic Low Back Pain in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes

brief_summary:
This study is a randomized controlled trial designed to investigate the effects of diaphragmatic breathing exercises and core stabilization exercises on symptom severity, quality of life, and sleep quality in patients with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).

Participants will be randomly allocated into three groups: a control group, a diaphragmatic breathing exercise group, and a combined diaphragmatic breathing and core stabilization exercise group. The intervention program will last for 8 weeks. Diaphragmatic breathing exercises will be performed 5 days per week, while core stabilization exercises will be performed 3 days per week.

Posture, body awareness, pain intensity, GERD-related symptoms, quality of life, and sleep quality will be assessed using validated measurement tools. The aim of the study is to compare the therapeutic effects of these exercise interventions on GERD-related outcomes and overall patient well-being.
primary_outcomes: The Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease Questionnaire (GERD-Q)
The PROMIS GERD Scale
The Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease Quality of Life Questionnaire (GERD-QOL)
Postural analysis
The Visual Analog Scale (VAS)
The Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI)
title: Effects of Breathing and Core Stabilization Exercises in Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease

brief_summary: This study compares rivaroxaban plus aspirin with aspirin alone in patients with stable coronary artery disease at high ischemic risk. The aim is to evaluate whether the combination therapy better prevents cardiovascular events and to assess its safety.
conditions: Stable Coronary Artery Disease (CAD), Myocardial Infarction
lead_sponsor: Republican Specialized Scientific and Practical Medical Center of Cardiology
primary_outcomes: Composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke
title: To Evaluate The Efficacy And Safety Of Rivaroxaban In Combination With Aspirin Compared With Aspirin Monotherapy In Patients With Stable Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) and High Ischemic Risk

brief_summary: This is a prospective, pre-post implementation study designed to evaluate how artificial intelligence-based selection committee (AI-SC) recommendations affect decision-making when integrated into routine clinical workflows. The study will focus on individual liver transplant candidacy decisions as the primary unit of analysis. Researchers will observe and analyze these decisions during weekly University Health Network (UHN) Liver Transplant Selection Committee meetings over an approximate 12-month period. The goal is to determine if the deployment of AI-SC recommendations changes, optimizes, or influences the committee's final transplant candidacy determinations compared to baseline practices.
primary_outcomes: Frequency of modification of transplant committee decisions after presentation of the AI-SC recommendation, measured as the proportion of cases in which the final post-AI decision differs from the recorded initial pre-AI decision
title: Prospective AI-SC Trial

brief_summary:
This study aims to investigate whether synchronizing accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation (aiTBS) with an individual's ongoing brain activity improves treatment outcomes in adults with Treatment-Resistant Depression (TRD).

Participants were randomly assigned to one of two treatment groups:

1. Phase-locked aiTBS (PL-aiTBS): Magnetic stimulation was synchronized with a specific phase of ongoing brain activity measured using electroencephalography (EEG).
2. Random-phase aiTBS (RP-aiTBS): Participants received the same stimulation protocol without synchronization to a specific phase of brain activity.

Both groups received personalized stimulation based on their individual theta frequency. Treatment consisted of 10 sessions over three consecutive days, with three sessions on Day 1, three sessions on Day 2, and four sessions on Day 3 (3-3-4 schedule). Each session delivered 1,800 magnetic pulses, resulting in a total of 18,000 pulses per participant.

The primary objective was to compare changes in depressive symptoms between the two treatment groups. Depression severity was assessed using the 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAM-D) and the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) at baseline (before the first stimulation session), mid-treatment (after the sixth session, Day 2), post-treatment (after the tenth session, Day 3), and follow-up (Day7).

Resting-state EEG recordings were collected before and after stimulation sessions to investigate treatment-related changes in neural oscillatory activity, phase-amplitude coupling, functional connectivity, and other neurophysiological measures, as well as their potential associations with improvements in depressive symptoms.
interventions: Phase-Locked Accelerated Intermittent Theta Burst Stimulation
Random-Phase Accelerated Intermittent Theta Burst Stimulation
primary_outcomes: Change in HAM-D Total Score
Change in MADRS Total Score
title: Phase-Locked Accelerated Intermittent Theta Burst Stimulation for Treatment-Resistant Depression

Eighteen patients undergoing fixed orthodontic treatment were randomly allocated into three groups: a control group using routine oral hygiene practices, a chlorhexidine mouthwash group, and a fluoride mouthwash group. A total of 36 orthodontic wire samples, comprising NiTi and stainless-steel archwires, were evaluated following one month of intraoral exposure.

Vickers microhardness, quantitative surface roughness, flexural modulus, kinetic friction, static friction, and surface morphology by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) were assessed before and after clinical exposure.

The data collected were statistically analyzed using appropriate statistical methods to compare the changes among different groups and between the two types of archwire materials.

This study aims to develop and evaluate an artificial intelligence (AI)-based system that can detect dental caries and dental plaque in children using intraoral digital scans and photographs, and use these findings to estimate each child's risk of developing dental caries.

Children aged 4-13 years who attend Marmara University Faculty of Dentistry, Department of Pediatric Dentistry for routine dental care will be invited to participate. Participants will receive a clinical dental examination. Dental caries will be evaluated using standard clinical criteria, and dental plaque will be assessed using a plaque index. Intraoral photographs and three-dimensional digital scans of the teeth will also be obtained. Parents will complete a questionnaire about their child's toothbrushing habits, sugar consumption, fluoride use, dental visits, and selected sociodemographic factors.

The collected digital images and scans will be used to train and test an AI model designed to automatically identify and measure areas of dental caries and plaque. The AI findings will then be combined with clinical examination results and oral health-related information to classify children as having low, moderate, or high caries risk.

Based on the assigned caries risk level, individualized preventive recommendations such as oral hygiene instruction, dietary counseling, fluoride applications, professional plaque control, and follow-up visits will be provided. Participants will be followed according to their risk level and digital scans and clinical assessments will be repeated to evaluate changes in caries, plaque, and caries risk over time.

The study is expected to provide information on whether AI-assisted digital imaging can support more objective, standardized and personalized caries risk assessment and preventive dental care in children.

This study evaluated the effectiveness of a university-level Flourishing Curriculum on students' well-being in Colombia using two rigorous designs: a cluster randomized study (Study 1, n = 389 control vs. n = 614 intervention) and an individually randomized controlled trial (Study 2, n = 77 control vs. n = 75 intervention). Both studies followed the same experimental and measurement structure. The nine-week-long curriculum integrated evidence-based components targeting meaning in life, forgiveness, humility, mindfulness, self-control, resilience, leadership, positive relationships, and spirituality, and was implemented within the standard academic course structure followed by students at the university. The control condition completed the measures but completed their usual coursework.

The assessment battery included Spanish-language versions of established psychological measures. These instruments had either been previously validated for use in Spanish-speaking populations or had been back-translated into Spanish by researchers at Universidad del Sinú for prior studies conducted in Colombia.

The investigators selected a set of 20 theory-driven and curriculum-informed outcome variables corresponding to two levels of anticipated change. First, investigators assessed constructs targeted by each of the nine curriculum modules, including coherence, purpose, and significance as three central dimensions of meaning in life, trait forgivingness, trait humility, mindfulness, self-control, resilience, leadership, loneliness, and transcendent spirituality. Second, constructs were assessed reflecting more distal outcomes that the flourishing curriculum is intended to support, including depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, stress overload, and a brief measure of multidimensional flourishing that yielded an overall flourishing score and five domain-specific scores: happiness and life satisfaction; mental and physical health; meaning and purpose; character and virtue; and close social relationships. Mean scores were computed for all outcome variables. In addition, following each module of the Flourishing Curriculum, students in the intervention group also completed a five-item course evaluation assessing satisfaction with the learning experience.
