brief_summary:
Chronic low back pain is a common condition that can affect a person's ability to move comfortably and perform everyday activities. Physiotherapy often includes exercises to improve the control and stability of the trunk muscles. However, the way patients are instructed to focus their attention during these exercises may influence how effectively they perform movements.

The purpose of this pilot study was to compare two types of instructions during abdominal bracing exercises in adults with chronic non-specific low back pain. Abdominal bracing involves tightening the abdominal muscles to support the trunk. The study compared an external focus of attention, where participants concentrated on the effects of their movements on external objects, with an internal focus of attention, where participants concentrated on movements of their own body.

Twelve adults aged 18-60 years with chronic non-specific low back pain participated in the study. They were randomly assigned to one of two groups. Both groups completed the same physiotherapy exercise program, consisting of eight supervised sessions over five weeks, with additional home exercises. The only difference between the groups was the type of instructions used during abdominal bracing.

In the external focus group, participants were instructed to concentrate on bringing small foam markers attached to their ribs toward their waistband. In the internal focus group, participants were instructed to concentrate on bringing their lower ribs toward their pelvis.

Participants were assessed before and after the intervention. The assessments included the speed of repeated trunk bending movements, trunk muscle endurance, pain intensity, limitations in daily activities, fear of movement, and sensitivity to pressure.

The study aimed to determine whether external focus instructions during abdominal bracing exercises could improve movement performance and clinical outcomes more effectively than internal focus instructions. The findings may help physiotherapists better understand how verbal instructions influence exercise performance and rehabilitation in people with chronic low back pain.
primary_outcomes: Repeated Trunk Flexion (RTF) Performance
title: External vs. Internal Focus During Abdominal Bracing in Low Back Pain

Both techniques involve injecting local anesthetic near nerves supplying the surgical area.

The study will include 78 adults aged 18 to 85 years undergoing elective mastectomy under general anesthesia. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive one of the two blocks before surgery. Both groups will receive postoperative pain treatment, including a patient-controlled device that delivers tramadol when needed.

The main aim is to compare postoperative opioid consumption. The study will also assess pain at rest and during movement, the need for additional pain medication, side effects, recovery quality, and persistent pain. Pain scores and tramadol consumption will be recorded at 0, 2, 4, 8, 16, and 24 hours after surgery. Recovery quality will be assessed at 24 hours, and persistent pain will be assessed by telephone at 3 months.

brief_summary:
Functional chronic constipation is a common digestive disorder in Chilean adults. It causes infrequent or difficult bowel movements, abdominal discomfort and a feeling of incomplete evacuation, and it can impair quality of life. Kefir is a fermented milk made with grains that contain lactic acid bacteria and yeasts. It has been proposed as a dietary option to relieve constipation, but its effects may depend on how it is prepared.

The purpose of this study is to evaluate whether daily intake of two homemade kefir formulations, one made with whole milk and one made with skim milk, improves constipation symptoms and quality of life in adults with functional chronic constipation, compared with dietary counseling alone.

Thirty adults of both sexes diagnosed with functional chronic constipation according to the Rome IV criteria will be randomly assigned to one of three groups (10 per group):

Whole-milk kefir (KLE) Skim-milk kefir (KLD) Control group receiving nutritional counseling based on the Chilean Dietary Guidelines only

Participants in the kefir groups will follow a gradual dose increase (50, 100, 150 and up to 200 mL/day) for 4 weeks. Both kefir formulations will be prepared under standardized conditions (6% grain inoculation, 48-hour fermentation) and characterized for their nutritional, microbiological and sensory properties before the trial.

The primary outcome will be constipation-specific quality of life, measured with the PAC-QOL questionnaire. Secondary outcomes will include constipation symptoms (Rome IV criteria), stool consistency (Bristol Stool Form Scale) and generic health-related quality of life (EQ-5D). Dietary intake (24-hour recall and food frequency questionnaire) and physical activity (GPAQ) will be recorded as potential confounders. All assessments will be done before and after the intervention.

The researchers expect that participants who drink kefir will improve their constipation symptoms and quality of life more than those who receive counseling only. They also expect a greater improvement with the whole-milk kefir
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in the Number of Rome IV Diagnostic Criteria for Functional Constipation Met at 1 Month
title: Pilot Study: Effectiveness of Different Kefir Formulations on Symptoms of Functional Constipation in Chilean Adults.

Cellbooster® Hair (CBH) is a class III medical device, CE marked, HA-based injectable using the patented CHAC Technology. It consists of stabilized Hyaluronic Acid 18mg (6mg/ml) with Amino Acids and Vitamins, and minerals (zinc, copper). The medical device is designed for strengthening hair follicles, improving hair growth and microcirculation. It restores scalp skin structure and provides hair fiber restructuring. The device is a resorbable injectable implant for preventing and treating various scalp and hair problems linked to hormonal imbalance, psoriasis, seborrhea, stress, nutrition and trace elements deficiencies, such as: hair loss, hair breakage, scalp dehydration, dandruff, premature graying. The device improves microcirculation, restores scalp skin structure and other qualities, provides hair fiber restructuring after physical and/or chemical damage, such as: hair dying, permanent wave, sun, dryer.

The current post-market clinical investigation aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of CBH in the scalp of subjects. For this purpose, healthy subjects with signs of hair loss will receive a 6-session treatment spaced every 2 weeks and will be followed-up over 130 days after the initial injection session. Objective measurements of scalp function and hair characteristics parameters will be performed allowing to assess hair density, hair diameter, hair structure, scalp hydration, scalp barrier function and thickness and having illustrative pictures. Subjective clinical improvement will be evaluated with clinical scoring, as well as subject and investigator satisfaction degrees. The safety of the injections will be assessed by collecting the Injection Site Reactions (ISRs) and Adverse Events (AEs).
primary_outcomes: Change from baseline of hair density (total number of hair in the studied zone) at Day 130 evaluated by Phototrichogram (PTG) analysis

A total of 2,872 patients will be enrolled from 14 Chinese centers. Participants will be stratified by surgery type, lymph node status, TNBC subtype, and neoadjuvant chemotherapy status. brief_summary:
Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a chronic, progressive, fibrosing interstitial lung disease that predominantly affects middle-aged and older adults. Progressive replacement of normal lung parenchyma by extracellular matrix and destruction of the alveolar architecture lead to reduced lung compliance and impaired gas exchange. Clinically, IPF is characterized by progressively worsening dyspnea, restrictive ventilatory impairment, impaired gas exchange, hypoxemia, and, in advanced cases, respiratory failure.

Current pharmacological treatment of IPF is primarily based on antifibrotic therapy. Pirfenidone and nintedanib were the first two antifibrotic agents approved for IPF and have been shown to slow the decline in forced vital capacity (FVC) through different mechanisms of action. Pirfenidone is an oral small-molecule agent with antifibrotic, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant properties. Although its mechanism of action has not been fully elucidated, it is thought to involve inhibition of transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β)-related signaling and suppression of fibroblast proliferation. Nintedanib is a multitarget tyrosine kinase inhibitor that inhibits several receptors involved in fibrotic pathways, including vascular endothelial growth factor receptors (VEGFRs), fibroblast growth factor receptors (FGFRs), and platelet-derived growth factor receptors (PDGFRs). More recently, nerandomilast, an oral phosphodiesterase 4B (PDE4B) inhibitor with anti-inflammatory and antifibrotic activity, has also been developed for the treatment of IPF.

Despite these therapeutic advances, currently available treatments mainly slow disease progression and do not reverse established pulmonary fibrosis or cure IPF. In addition, treatment may be limited by adverse reactions and tolerability issues. Common adverse reactions associated with pirfenidone include gastrointestinal symptoms, photosensitivity reactions, and rash, while diarrhea is a frequent adverse reaction associated with nintedanib. Therefore, there remains an unmet medical need for novel therapies with improved efficacy and an acceptable safety and tolerability profile.

ND-003, formerly known as ND003, is a novel small-molecule compound jointly developed by Shenzhen Xinyue Biotechnology Co., Ltd. and Shenzhen Small Molecule Innovative Drug Center Co., Ltd. for the treatment of pulmonary fibrosis. ND-003 is a kinase inhibitor targeting discoidin domain receptor 1 (DDR1), colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor (CSF1R), and platelet-derived growth factor receptor beta (PDGFR-β). By selectively interacting with these targets and modulating signaling pathways involved in fibrotic processes, ND-003 is intended to inhibit or delay the progression of tissue fibrosis.

The primary objective of this study is to evaluate the preliminary efficacy of ND-003 tablets in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and to provide scientific evidence to support dose selection for subsequent clinical development. The study will also evaluate the safety and tolerability of ND-003 tablets in patients with IPF.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants with a ≥10% decline in forced vital capacity (FVC) from baseline.
title: A Phase Ⅱa Study of ND-003 Tablets in Patients With Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis

brief_summary:
Introduction: Interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome (IC/BPS) is a disease of unknown etiology, with clinical characteristics of bladder pain, frequency, urgency, and nocturia. There has been no effective and durable medication to cure this disease. Current research has revealed that chronic bladder wall inflammation and bladder mucosal denudation are the fundamental pathology for clinical symptoms. Using Jing Si Herbal Tea liquid packets may have a therapeutic effect in patients with refractory IC/BPS.

Aim: To investigate the effect of Jing Si Herbal Tea liquid packet intervention added to urological therapy for patients with refractory IC/BPS.

Materials and Methods: This study will enroll patients with IC/BPS who are refractory to various conventional treatments after cystoscopic hydrodistention, antimuscarinic, and painkiller treatments. These patients plan to receive further intravesical IC therapy, such as intravesical hyaluronic acid (HA) instillation, intravesical botulinum toxin A (Botox) injection, intravesical platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injection, or low-energy shock wave (LESW) therapy. The patients will be randomly assigned to receive intravesical IC therapy and placebo (control group) or concomitant IC treatment with Jing Si Herbal Tea liquid packet TID (treatment group) for 3 months. The voiding diary, ICSI, ICPI, VAS, PPBC, GRA, Qmax, Vol, and PVR are also assessed at baseline and at 4, 12, and 20 weeks after treatment. The primary endpoint of this study is the improvement of GRA by 2 points at 12 weeks after treatment.

Assessment: The patients will be investigated using the voiding diary (for frequency of nocturia episodes per day), ICSI, IC problem index (ICPI), Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) of pain, patient perception of bladder condition (PPBC), global response assessment (GRA), maximal flow rate (Qmax), voided volume (Vol), and post-void residual urine (PVR) volume measurement at baseline and after treatment. Urine samples will also be obtained for determination of urinary biomarkers at baseline and after different therapies.
interventions: Jing Si Herbal Tea liquid packet
primary_outcomes: Global Response Assessment (GRA) at Week 12
title: Clinical Efficacy of Jing Si Herbal Tea Liquid Packet to Treat Patients With Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome

brief_summary:
Emerging adulthood is a developmental phase situated between adolescence and adulthood, characterized by an intensive process of identity formation, the pursuit of independence, the assumption of responsibilities, and decision-making regarding the future. During this period, individuals encounter significant changes across various domains, including their educational journey, career planning, social relationships, and economic independence. In addition to the developmental characteristics inherent to emerging adulthood, nursing students face professional stressors such as a heavy academic workload, clinical practicums, direct involvement in patient care, responsibilities concerning patient safety, and the fear of making errors. The literature indicates that nursing students experience higher levels of stress, anxiety, and psychological distress compared to university students in other disciplines. Consequently, the psychological well-being and a robust sense of self/identity among nursing students are of critical importance-both for the students themselves and for the individuals under their care. Given the implications for human and public health, the significance of research, projects, and investments in this area is evident.

This study is designed to evaluate the impact of Hatha Yoga practice on the self-perception and psychological well-being of nursing students in the stage of emerging adulthood. The study will be conducted within the Department of Nursing at the Faculty of Health Sciences, Afyonkarahisar Health Sciences University. The sample will consist of nursing students who meet the inclusion criteria and consent to participate in the study. Participants will be divided into two groups: an intervention group and a control group. The sample size was calculated using the G\*Power 3.1.9 software; accounting for potential attrition, the study is planned to be conducted with a total of 60 participants, consisting of 30 individuals in the intervention group and 30 in the control group. Students in the intervention group will engage in Hatha yoga for eight weeks, following a structured program, while students in the control group will continue with their routine educational activities without receiving any intervention. Data will be collected at three distinct time points: before the intervention, immediately after the intervention, and three months post-intervention. The instruments used for data collection will include a "Descriptive Information Form," the "Multidimensional Self-Perception Scale," and the "Psychological Well-Being Scale." The primary outcomes of the study are the students' self-perception and levels of psychological well-being. Data obtained from the study will be analyzed using the SPSS software package.
primary_outcomes: Self-perception
Psychological Well-Being
title: EFFECT OF HATHA YOGA ON SELF-PERCEPTION AND PSYCHOLOGICAL WELL-BEING IN NURSING STUDENTS

brief_summary:
This multicenter study will evaluate whether adding cardiac coherence breathing sessions to continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) improves sleep quality in adults with newly diagnosed obstructive sleep apnea who are starting CPAP. Approximately 180 participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. Both groups will start treatment with the HALOA CPAP system. In one group, the cardiac coherence module will be activated at the start of treatment. In the other group, participants will use CPAP alone for 8 weeks before the module is activated.

Sleep quality will be assessed at study entry, at 8 weeks, and at 16 weeks using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. The primary comparison will assess the change in sleep quality from study entry to week 8 between the two groups. Secondary assessments will include daytime sleepiness, insomnia symptoms, anxiety and depression symptoms, treatment satisfaction, usability of the cardiac coherence module, CPAP use, and heart-rate variability when polysomnography recordings are available.
primary_outcomes: Change in Global Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) Score

brief_summary:
Every year, a lot of NHS medicine goes to waste. This can happen for many reasons. Sometimes treatment plans might change. Sometimes patients get side-effects. Sadly, some patients die before they finish their medicine. Even if medicines are still in date and unopened, UK rules say they must be thrown away. This is because we can't tell if they've been stored safely and are still okay to use.

Wasting medicines is harmful in many ways. Making and moving medicines creates more pollution than all the cars on the road. When unused medicines are thrown away, they can leak into soil and water, damaging the environment. It's also expensive. This waste costs the NHS over £300 million every year. Also, when we throw away medicines that could have been reused, it can cause medicine shortages, making it harder for others to get the treatments they need.

This project will test a new medicine bag called the PharmaBag which can tell if a medicine has been opened or kept too hot or too cold. If an unopened medicine is returned in a PharmaBag, and it has been stored safely, it might be possible to safely reuse it. This could be especially important for expensive cancer medicines, which are often left unused due to side effects or treatment changes.

We will give patients who are prescribed oral anti-cancer medicines their normal prescription inside the PharmaBags. This will help us see how well the bags work in real NHS settings. Exercise therapy is considered a first-line treatment; however, some patients continue to experience pain and functional limitations despite rehabilitation.

This treatment may help reduce pain and improve shoulder function when combined with therapeutic exercise.

The purpose of this randomized controlled trial is to investigate whether adding ultrasound-guided percutaneous electrolysis to a structured exercise rehabilitation program provides greater improvements in shoulder pain and disability than exercise therapy alone in adults with chronic supraspinatus tendinopathy.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. Both groups will complete a six-week exercise program involving progressive shoulder strengthening, eccentric exercises, and scapular stabilization. Participants in the experimental group will additionally receive one session of ultrasound-guided percutaneous electrolysis per week for six weeks.

Shoulder pain and disability will be evaluated before and after the intervention using the Shoulder Pain and Disability Index (SPADI). Additional assessments will include pain intensity, shoulder range of motion, pain-related self-efficacy, and adverse events.

The investigators hypothesize that combining ultrasound-guided percutaneous electrolysis with exercise therapy will produce greater improvements in shoulder pain, disability, and functional outcomes compared with exercise therapy alone.

brief_summary: This phase III trial compares the effect of a shorter duration (hypofractionated) of intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) with brachytherapy and cisplatin to standard duration IMRT with brachytherapy and cisplatin in treating patients with newly diagnosed stage IB2-IIIC1 cervical cancer. Cisplatin is in a class of medications known as platinum-containing compounds. It works by killing, stopping or slowing the growth of tumor cells. Radiation therapy uses high energy x-rays, particles, or radioactive seeds to kill tumor cells and shrink tumors. IMRT is a type of 3-dimensional radiation therapy that uses computer-generated images to show the size and shape of the tumor. Thin beams of radiation of different intensities are aimed at the tumor from many angles. This type of radiation therapy reduces the damage to healthy tissue near the tumor. Hypofractionated radiation therapy delivers higher doses of radiation therapy over a shorter period of time and may kill more tumor cells and have fewer side effects. A radiation boost is extra radiation to the area where the tumor is located which increases the amount of radiation given to the tumor bed. Brachytherapy, also known as internal radiation therapy, uses radioactive material placed directly into or near a tumor to kill tumor cells. Giving hypofractionated chemoradiation therapy may be as safe, tolerable and/or effective as the standard, longer course of chemoradiation therapy in treating patients newly diagnosed with stage IB2-IIIC1 cervical cancer.

brief_summary: Escape rooms are an entertainment activity that typically involves a team of two or more people. It was carried out during the 2024-25 academic year with second-year students enrolled on the "Emergency Response in Unusual Situations" course on the Paramedic (First and Emergency Aid) programme at a health services vocational school in Turkey. A total population sampling method was employed, meaning no specific sample selection process was used. Randomisation was stratified by the students' respective academic tracks: those in the evening programme formed the intervention group (n = 33), while those in the daytime programme formed the control group (n = 36). Data were collected after a theoretical lecture using a personal information form, a knowledge test and the "Emergency Medical Technician Professional Competence Perception Scale" (administered as a pre-test). Two weeks after the theoretical instruction, an "Emergency Intervention" escape room simulation focused on burn care and emergency response was conducted in a laboratory setting for the intervention group. Participants were organised into three-person teams and guided through specific scenarios. No such activity was implemented for the control group. Both groups then completed the knowledge test and the "Emergency Medical Technician Professional Competence Perception Scale" as a post-test. The analysis of the data used descriptive statistical methods, the independent samples t-test, the Mann-Whitney U test, the Kruskal-Wallis test, the paired samples t-test and the Wilcoxon signed-rank test.
primary_outcomes: Differences of knowledge scores between groups
title: ESCAPE ROOM FOR PARAMEDIC STUDENTS

brief_summary:
The HEART application is designed to support the implementation of secondary prevention, as well as the second and third (lifelong) phases of cardiac rehabilitation, in a broad spectrum of patients with chronic coronary syndromes following cardiovascular events (including acute myocardial infarction, angina pectoris, and coronary interventions).

The application has been registered with the Intellectual Property Office of the Republic of Serbia, with the Institute for Cardiovascular Diseases Dedinje as the rights holder. It was developed as a Proof-of-Concept project through a collaboration between the Institute for Cardiovascular Diseases Dedinje and the World Bank. The initiation of an academic study is planned pending approval from the Institute's Ethics Committee.

Following the provision of highly specialized care in tertiary referral centers, such as the Institute for Cardiovascular Diseases Dedinje, patients are typically referred to local healthcare institutions for continued follow-up and long-term management. However, real-world data indicate that post-discharge care is often suboptimal. Patients frequently demonstrate poor adherence to prescribed therapies and inadequate control of cardiovascular risk factors, resulting in a substantial risk of rehospitalization. Notably, up to 20% of patients experience a recurrent cardiovascular event within the first year after discharge.

These gaps in care are driven by multiple factors operating at different levels: at the healthcare system level, there is a limited availability of structured secondary prevention programs; at the provider level, referral rates to cardiac rehabilitation-particularly inpatient programs-remain low; and at the patient level, barriers include limited awareness, geographical distance, financial constraints, and other socioeconomic factors.

The secondary prevention and cardiac rehabilitation program encompass a comprehensive set of interventions aimed at recovery and reintegration into daily life immediately following a cardiovascular event.

Our digital platform represents the first designed hybrid model in Serbia and the wider region, accessible to any patient with a smartphone or computer access. It provides structured support for recovery and return to everyday life in a home-based setting following a cardiovascular event. The platform promotes active patient engagement in health management and encourages continuous monitoring of activities that contribute to reducing the risk of recurrent cardiovascular events, complications, and rehospitalizations, while also enabling improvements in quality of life.

It is designed as an individualized program focused on enhancing functional capacity, patient education, and ongoing support. The platform systematically monitors the modification of cardiovascular risk factors, lifestyle changes, adherence to prescribed therapy, and the achievement of optimal and target clinical values.

The platform is designed to allow the physician, at discharge or during an outpatient visit, to enter relevant patient data, including the presence of cardiovascular risk factors, secondary prevention targets, and key information from the medical record. The patient is then provided with secure access credentials to the platform via a mobile application or web portal.

Patients will receive instructions on how to use the application, which is intended for educational purposes and is non-interventional, meaning it does not provide independent guidance on therapy modification or management of acute conditions.

Patients will be required to input data related to diet, lifestyle, physical activity, medication adherence, and laboratory test results.

Follow-up visits will be scheduled at 4-6 weeks after enrollment and subsequently as needed, depending on risk factor control, for a total follow-up period of up to one year.

The platform includes educational materials as well as guided warm-up, stretching, and cool-down exercises, promoting physical activity in accordance with the principles of the European Society of Cardiology.

Patients will also be invited to provide feedback on the application's design and functionality, including comments and suggestions, as part of a user satisfaction assessment.
primary_outcomes: Time to First Occurrence of a Major Adverse Cardiovascular Event (MACE)
title: Holistic Empowerment Assistance Recovery Transformation

They are rapid, cost-effective, and sensitive techniques; however, they may cause local discomfort and itching (pruritus), which can be particularly distressing for children.

In pediatric nursing, improving patient comfort and reducing anxiety are key priorities. Various interventions, including topical corticosteroids, ice, and cold, wet compresses, have been used to relieve itching, but none has been shown to effectively reduce pruritus following skin prick testing. Available evidence suggests that post-prick test itching usually resolves spontaneously and that topical corticosteroids have not demonstrated clear superiority over simple interventions. A total of 100 children will be enrolled and randomly allocated to one of two groups: (A) an intervention group, which will receive Ceramol Beta Complex® cream, or (B) a control group, which will receive the emollient cream routinely used in our pediatric allergy clinics
interventions: The control group will receive an emollient cream (B), prepared by the hospital pharmacy, without antipruritic or soothing ingredients.

brief_summary:
The goal of this prospective case series is to assess the feasibility of intervention and assessment protocols for telehealth intervention with mindfulness-based exercise, transcranial direct current stimulation, and their combination in Veterans with peristent post-traumatic headache. The main questions it aims to answer are:

What percentage of patients complete pre- and post- assessment measures? Are patients adherent to and satisfied with each intervention? What are potential adverse effects of treatment? How responsive are patient-reported outcome measures and biomarkers of brain connectivity, muscle health, and pain sensitivity to change following treatment?

Participants will complete 18 telehealth sessions with a physical therapist (3x/wk for 6 weeks) with one of the following interventions:

1. mindfulness-based cervicoscapular exercise
2. transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) over the motor cortex
3. combined treatment with exercise and tDCS

A total of 72 participants will be allocated into two groups. Both groups will receive a standard TAP block using bupivacaine and dexamethasone, while the intervention group will additionally receive magnesium sulfate.

The primary outcome of the study is the early quality of recovery assessed at 24 hours postoperatively. Secondary outcomes include postoperative pain scores, total opioid consumption, time to first rescue analgesia, the incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting, patient satisfaction, block-related complications, intraoperative opioid requirements, hemodynamic parameters, and the incidence of chronic postoperative pain assessed through six months of follow-up.

brief_summary:
Supraglottic airway devices (SADs) like the i-gel are frequently used to manage airways during general anesthesia in children. However, delivering positive-pressure mechanical ventilation through a supraglottic airway carries a risk of gas leaking around the cuff into the stomach (gastric insufflation), which can cause stomach distension and increase the risk of regurgitation.

Volume-controlled ventilation (VCV) delivers a fixed breath volume, which can cause spikes in peak inspiratory pressure if airway resistance changes, potentially exceeding the device seal and forcing air into the stomach. Pressure-controlled ventilation with volume guarantee (PCV-VG) uses closed-loop feedback to auto-titrate inspiratory pressure breath-by-breath to target the desired tidal volume while minimizing peak airway pressures.

This prospective, single-center, randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate whether PCV-VG offers superior ventilatory efficacy (accurate tidal volume delivery) and enhanced gastric safety (lower incidence of ultrasonographically detected gastric insufflation) compared to VCV when using the i-gel supraglottic airway in children aged 2 to 7 years undergoing elective non-laparoscopic surgery
primary_outcomes: Mean Expired Tidal Volume (VTe) Delivery Accuracy
Percentage of Participants With Ultrasonographically Confirmed Gastric Insufflation
title: PCV-VG Versus VCV Through the I-gel in Young Children

brief_summary:
Prefrontal cortical dysfunction in patients with schizophrenia (SCZ) may result from impaired thalamic inputs to this region. Meanwhile, patients with SCZ exhibit a reduced GABA/glutamate ratio in the thalamus, indicating thalamic excitation/inhibition (E/I) imbalance. In addition, SCZ patients show marked reduction of sleep spindles, which are predominantly generated by the thalamic reticular nucleus. Therefore, thalamus-targeted temporal interference stimulation (TIS) may modulate the function of thalamocortical circuits, ameliorate clinical symptoms including cognitive deficits in patients with SCZ, and serve as an effective non-pharmacological intervention. This study consists of two trial components with three objectives: (1) to explore the therapeutic effect of TIS on cognitive function in patients with SCZ; (2) to explore the effect of TIS on positive symptoms in patients with SCZ; (3) to investigate the neural mechanisms underlying TIS-mediated symptom modulation in SCZ.

Trial 1: This study adopts a randomized, controlled, crossover design. Participants will be randomly assigned to two groups: Group A and Group B. Clinical data from 30 patients with schizophrenia (15 participants per group) will be collected, including baseline clinical rating scale scores, cognitive assessments, electroencephalography (EEG), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data. All participants will receive two sessions of TIS intervention in a crossover fashion, with a 1-week washout period between the two interventions. One day prior to each TIS session, participants will complete two training runs of the Sternberg Item-Recognition Paradigm (SIRP) to eliminate confounding learning effects. Outcome measurements including clinical scale scores, cognitive assessments, EEG and MRI data will be acquired at baseline. Task-state MRI will be recorded during both stimulation sessions.

Trial 2: This trial uses a rigorous randomized controlled design. Participants will be randomized into two arms: the TIS group and the control group. Fifty patients with schizophrenia will be enrolled (25 participants per group). Baseline data will be collected, including clinical symptom ratings, cognitive function scores, EEG-derived E/I imbalance metrics, and MRI data. The intervention lasts for 2 weeks with twice-daily stimulation, totaling 20 sessions. Assessments will be performed at baseline, at the end of the 2-week intervention, and at a 4-week post-intervention follow-up to evaluate changes in clinical symptoms, cognition, EEG E/I imbalance, and brain structural and functional features. This trial aims to explore the short-term efficacy, safety, and neurobiological mechanisms of TIS for improving cognitive function in schizophrenia.
primary_outcomes: Changes in brain function
changes on the MATRICS Consensus Cognitive Battery (MCCB) scores
title: Temporal Interference Stimulation Targeting Thalamus for Schizophrenia-Related Cognitive Dysfunction

brief_summary:
This randomized crossover trial investigated whether brief, one-minute bouts of exercise, known as "exercise snacks," could improve daytime blood glucose levels in adults with type 2 diabetes who were not receiving insulin treatment. The study also examined whether increasing the number of daily exercise snacks provided additional benefits for blood glucose control.

Participants were randomly assigned to different sequences of four experimental conditions: no prescribed exercise snacks (CON), four exercise snacks per day (ES4), six exercise snacks per day (ES6), and eight exercise snacks per day (ES8). Each condition lasted two consecutive days, with a washout period of at least 72 hours between conditions. Each exercise snack consisted of one minute of vigorous body-weight movements. Three exercise sessions were scheduled after meals, while additional sessions were performed at other times of the day.

Participants followed standardized meal plans and wore continuous glucose monitoring devices to measure glucose levels throughout the study. The primary outcome was mean daytime sensor glucose from 6:00 AM to midnight. Additional assessments included glucose variability, post-meal glucose responses, physical activity, exercise adherence, participant acceptability, and safety.

The researchers hypothesized that at least one exercise snack condition would reduce daytime glucose compared with the control condition, while additional daily exercise sessions might not necessarily produce greater glucose-lowering benefits. The findings were intended to inform practical, time-efficient exercise recommendations for adults with type 2 diabetes.

primary_outcomes: Mean Daytime Sensor Glucose (06:00-24:00)
title: One-Minute Exercise Snacks and Daytime Glucose in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes

brief_summary:
This small pilot study will assess whether early pregnancy loss (miscarriage) can be treated in an outpatient clinic using hysteroscopy without anesthesia, how well patients tolerate the procedure, and what complications occur. Hysteroscopy uses a small-diameter instrument with a camera to see inside the womb (uterus). A tissue removal device allows the doctor to remove pregnancy tissue while watching it directly.

The study will enroll 20 patients with pregnancy loss at up to 8 weeks of pregnancy who have chosen surgical treatment over medical treatment or expectant management. All participants will receive the study procedure; there is no comparison group. Researchers will record whether the pregnancy tissue is completely removed, pain during and shortly after the procedure, procedure duration, and complications. If the procedure cannot be completed or a participant asks to stop because of discomfort, an alternative procedure using suction aspiration (i.e., the traditional procedure for surgical abortion) will be offered the same day under sedation.

Participants will be invited to a follow-up visit 4-6 weeks later. This visit will include an ultrasound scan and diagnostic hysteroscopy to check for remaining pregnancy tissue or scar tissue inside the womb. The findings will provide an initial assessment of this approach and help guide future research.
interventions: Operative hysteroscopy using the tissue removal device
primary_outcomes: Procedural success
title: Operative Hysteroscopic Using a Tissue Removal Device for Surgical Management of Early Pregnancy Loss Without Anesthesia - A Pilot Study

brief_summary:
This study is designed to evaluate the efficacy of Relugolix for 3 months before radical prostatectomy + lymph node dissection followed by 6 months Relugolix versus radical prostatectomy + lymphnode dissection followed by 6 months Relugolix. Relugolix is an oral highly selective LHRH antagonist given daily that has been shown to achieve androgen deprivation in both phase I and phase II trials and was finally approved in the phase III HERO trial.

Relugolix is approved in the United States (US) and Europe for the treatment of advanced prostate cancer.

The HERO trial enrolled patients with castration sensitive prostate cancer and compared their sustained castration rate at 48weeks to leuprolide. While the safety profile of the 2 agents was similar, relugolix achieved castrate levels of testosterone faster and provided a higher overall rate of castration. In the phase III HERO trial, relugolix demonstrated suppression of testosterone concentrations to castration levels in 96.7% of patients from Day 29 through 48 weeks, which was superior to leuprolide and resulted in a 54% lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular events. Relugolix also demonstrated superior efficacy to leuprolide for key secondary endpoints, including the cumulative probability of testosterone suppression to castrate levels (\< 50 ng/dL) on day 4 and on day 15, PSA response (\> 50% decrease) at day 15 with confirmation at day 29, the cumulative probability of testosterone suppression to profound castrate levels (\< 20 ng/dL) on day 15, and mean FSH level at the end of week 24. Testosterone recovery was investigated in a subgroup of patients (n = 184): 54% of relugolix recipients versus 3% of leuprolide recipients had testosterone recovery to ≥ 280 ng/dL 90 days after completing 48 weeks of treatment.Relugolix was generally well tolerated in men with prostate cancer, with most adverse events being consistent with physiologic effects of testosterone suppression. Most adverse events were of grade 1 or 2 severity. In a phase II study comparing relugolix to degarelix the global health status, as assessed by EORTC-QLQ-C30, and sexual activity and hormonal treatment-related symptoms, as assessed by the EORTC-QLQ-PR25, were negatively affected during treatment in both groups. Within 12 wk after treatment discontinuation, sexual activity scores improved by a mean of 12.1 for relugolix and 6.6 for degarelix and hormonal treatment-related symptoms changed by a mean of -5.0 and -1, respectively. Similarly, AMS total and subscale scores (sexual, psychological, and somatic) worsened during treatment in both groups but after treatment discontinuation, the mean percentage change in AMS total scores was -15% in the relugolix group and -2.9% in the degarelix group.

The fast testosterone recovery with relugolix was associated with a rapid improvement in a range of castration-related symptoms on QoL measures.

Building upon the practice-changing evidence established by the PROTEUS trial, evaluating oral Relugolix as a perioperative backbone in high-risk patients candidate for radical prostatectomy offers distinct pharmacological, safety, and patient-centered advantages. While PROTEUS validated the clinical benefit of perioperative androgen receptor pathway modulation, Relugolix provides rapid and profound testosterone suppression without an initial surge, paired with a significantly lower cardiovascular risk profile and markedly accelerated post-treatment testosterone and Quality of Life (QoL) recovery compared to standard LHRH agonists. In the HEROIC trial, testing a 3-month neoadjuvant Relugolix induction phase prior to surgery followed by 6 months of adjuvant Relugolix (Arm A) versus immediate surgery followed by 6 months of adjuvant Relugolix (Arm B) addresses whether an all-oral GnRH antagonist strategy can reproduce perioperative oncological downstaging and improve Biochemical Recurrence-Free Survival (bRFS) while optimizing cardiovascular safety and patient recovery.
primary_outcomes: Biochemical Recurrence-Free Survival (bRFS)
title: Relugolix in Patients With High-risk, Localized or Locally Advanced Prostate Cancer Who Are Candidates for Radical Prostatectomy.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the effects of a nurse-led, structured risk factor management programme on health-related quality of life, symptom burden and cardiovascular health in adults with atrial fibrillation (AF).

AF is the most common heart rhythm disorder. It increase the risk of stroke, heart failure, and death. Its symptoms, including palpitation, fatigue, and breathlessness, often limit daily activities and reduce quality of life, even in patients receiving treatment to control heart rhythm or rate. in the proposed nurse-led program, the cardiac nurse will teach AF patients how to manage health habits that affect AF, including eating well, staying active, sleeping well, not smoking, drinking less alcohol, and taking medicines as prescribed. A nurse works with each person to set small, realistic goals.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Does the programme improve health-related quality of life for AF patients?
2. Does the programme improve symptom burden for AF patients?
3. Does the programme improve the functional exercise capacity for AF patients?
4. Does the programme increase the reported self-efficacy level for participants?
5. Does the programme improve the health behaviours, physiological risk parameters and cardiovascular health score for participants?

Researcher will compare interventional group (80 AF participants joining the 12-week program in addition to usual care) to a control group (80 AF participants receive usual care only) to see if the program works to improve the quality of life, symptom burden and overall cardiovascular health than usual care alone among AF patients.

Participants in the intervention group will:

1. Receive a 1-hour face-to-face individual session with nurse for structured AF self-management education and personalized behavioural change planning in week 1
2. Keep track of their own health behaviours using a self-management booklet
3. Get 6 bi-weekly telephone follow-up calls from the nurse to review progress and support staged behavioural change
4. Receive weekly tailored text messages with reminders and encouragement

The study will take place at three hospitals in Hong Kong and will enrol about 160 adults. Each person will take part for about 5 months. Researchers will evaluate outcome (quality of life, AF symptom severity, functional exercise capacity, self-efficacy, health behaviours, body mass index, blood pressure, blood cholesterol, blood sugar, Life Essential 8 score) at three timepoint: baseline, upon completion of the programme (12 week), and 8 weeks thereafter (20 week).
interventions: A nurse-led, structured risk factor management programme for AF patients
primary_outcomes: Health-related quality of life assessed by Atrial Fibrillation Effect on Quality-of-Life (AFEQT)
title: A Nurse-led Structured Risk Factor Management Programme to Improve Quality of Life for Patients With Atrial Fibrillation

brief_summary:
Pregnancy involves substantial physical and emotional changes. During the first trimester, women may experience various pregnancy-related symptoms and anxiety as they adapt to pregnancy. These symptoms and concerns may affect their daily lives and overall well-being. Laughter yoga and progressive muscle relaxation are non-pharmacological approaches that may help women cope with these experiences.

This randomized controlled study aims to examine the effects of laughter yoga and progressive muscle relaxation exercises on pregnancy symptoms and pregnancy-related anxiety among primiparous women in the first trimester. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: laughter yoga, progressive muscle relaxation, or control. Women in the intervention groups will participate in structured online sessions of laughter yoga or progressive muscle relaxation exercises, while women in the control group will continue their routine care. Pregnancy symptoms and pregnancy-related anxiety will be assessed at baseline, Day 30, and Day 60. The study will compare changes in these outcomes across the three groups to determine the effects of the interventions.
primary_outcomes: Pregnancy Symptoms Inventory (PSI)
Pregnancy-Related Anxiety Questionnaire (PRAQ)
title: The Effects of Laughter Yoga and Progressive Muscle Relaxation Exercises on Pregnancy Symptoms and Pregnancy-Related Anxiety in Primiparous Women in the First Trimester

brief_summary:
Diabetes can slow down stomach emptying. As a result, some patients with diabetes may still have food or fluid in their stomach before surgery, even after following standard fasting rules. This can increase the risk of stomach contents entering the lungs (pulmonary aspiration) during anesthesia.

The aim of this prospective observational study is to measure the amount of residual stomach content using bedside gastric ultrasound in adult patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes scheduled for elective surgery under general anesthesia. The study will also determine how often a high aspiration risk is present and identify clinical factors associated with it, including HbA1c level, duration of diabetes, use of GLP-1 receptor agonists, insulin use, fasting duration, and gastroparesis symptoms.

Gastric ultrasound is non-invasive, painless, and does not involve radiation. No drug or additional intervention will be given as part of this study. Patients found to be at high aspiration risk will be reported to the responsible anesthesiologist.
lead_sponsor: Saglik Bilimleri Universitesi Gazi Yasargil Training and Research Hospital
primary_outcomes: Residual Gastric Volume Assessed by Preoperative Gastric Ultrasound
title: Preoperative Gastric Ultrasound to Assess Stomach Contents and Aspiration Risk in Patients With Diabetes

brief_summary:
Gynecological examinations are important for women's health, but they may cause anxiety, fear, discomfort, and pain. This study aims to evaluate whether mandala coloring before a gynecological examination can reduce anxiety, fear, and pain perception in women.

This randomized controlled trial will include 60 women aged 18-50 years attending the Gynecology and Obstetrics Outpatient Clinic at Artvin State Hospital in Türkiye. Participants will be randomly assigned to two groups. Women in the intervention group will complete a brief mandala coloring activity before their examination, while women in the control group will wait without receiving the intervention.

Anxiety, fear, and pain will be assessed using the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory and Visual Analog Scales at specified assessment points before and after the intervention or waiting period and following the gynecological examination.

The study will help determine whether mandala coloring can be used as a simple, low-cost, non-pharmacological supportive method to improve women's experiences during gynecological examinations.
primary_outcomes: Change in State Anxiety (STAI-S) Score Before Gynecological Examination
title: Effects of Mandala Coloring Before Gynecological Examination on Anxiety, Fear, and Pain

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized controlled trial in Southern Chad is to learn if family planning social marketing activities can improve sexual and reproductive health, education and empowerment among women aged 15-49 years old. Planned activities include health provider training, partnership with private clinics, community midwife outreach, support to private pharmacies and retailers, and activities to raise awareness of family planning among the general population. The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Do these activities increase the proportion of women using a modern contraceptive method, and in particular the proportion using their preferred method?
2. Can these activities reduce unintended pregnancies and intimate partner violence, and improve autonomy, empowerment, child health and education?
3. What are the economic costs of doing these activities?
4. How cost-effective are these activities, given their potential impact on health and empowerment outcomes?
5. To what extent are these activities being implemented according to the original plan and timeline?

Researchers will compare women living in the areas receiving the social marketing intervention activities (intervention arm) to women living in areas not receiving these activities (control arm) to see to what extent health and empowerment outcomes differ between the two arms.

In intervention areas, the implementing partner DKT International will conduct the following activities:

* visiting pharmacies to encourage them to stock DKT-branded contraceptives
* training public and private sector healthcare providers
* partnering with existing private clinics to provide training and commodity support
* organizing subsidized contraceptive access days for the community.
* training midwives to provide contraceptives in remote communities
* advertising contraceptives on billboards, radio, pharmacies, social media and digital channels
* advertising DKT's regional call center
* organizing public events
* community mobilization by community health workers.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Women Using (or Whose Partner Uses) a Modern Contraceptive Method (mCPR)
Proportion of Women Whose Contraceptive Use or Non-Use Is Concordant with Their Fertility Preferences (Preference-Aligned Fertility Management)
title: Estimating the Impact of Family Planning Social Marketing Activities on Reproductive Health and Empowerment Outcomes in Chad: A Randomized Controlled Trial for the Family Planning Impact Lab

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether an antibiotic-releasing nail placed inside the shinbone (tibia) helps prevent infection and supports bone healing in adults with an open shinbone fracture. The study will test two versions of the Reselution Tibial Intramedullary Fixation System: one that releases vancomycin (Reselution V) and one that releases vancomycin and tobramycin (Reselution VT).

The main question it aims to answer is: within 12 months of surgery, how many participants heal without unplanned repeat surgery on the injured leg, have a healed bone on X-ray, and have no serious device-related side effects?

Participants will:

* Have surgery to fix their shinbone with the Reselution nail
* Have blood tests in the first 2 weeks after surgery (this testing may be stopped for later participants after an independent safety review)
* Attend follow-up visits for up to 24 months, including X-rays and questionnaires
interventions: Reselution V Tibial Intramedullary Fixation System
Reselution VT Tibial Intramedullary Fixation System
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants With Composite Success at 12 Months
title: Local Antibiotic Delivery From an Intramedullary Nail After Surgical Treatment of Tibial Fractures at High Risk of Infection

brief_summary: This study aims to determine the effect of long-term head and neck venous outflow obstruction-specifically internal jugular vein stenosis (IJVS) caused by atlas transverse process compression with a stenosis rate ≥50%-on cognitive function, and to observe the cognitive outcomes of atlas transverse process resection combined with release and perfusion technique in routine clinical care. The study uses a case-control design to compare cognitive function between patients with IJVS and matched healthy controls, and a prospective cohort design to follow surgical and non-surgical cohorts for 6 months. The Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) total score is the primary cognitive measure. The target population per the protocol summary is image-confirmed IJVS due to atlas transverse process compression (stenosis ≥50%), with mild-to-moderate cognitive impairment (MoCA \<26), aged 18-65 years.
lead_sponsor: Beijing Shijitan Hospital, Capital Medical University
primary_outcomes: Change in MoCA total score
title: Effect of Long-Term Head and Neck Venous Outflow Obstruction on Cognitive Function: Evidence From Patients With Internal Jugular Vein Stenosis

brief_summary: This study will be conducted under routine clinical practice in adults diagnosed with advanced chronic renal failure for whom treatment with Kremezin immediate-release tablets or Kremezin fine granules has been determined as part of standard clinical care. Kremezin will be prescribed and administered in accordance with the approved product labeling. Study data will be collected at up to three time points through Week 48: baseline, Week 24, and Week 48. Effectiveness will be assessed using serum creatinine (Scr), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and the investigator's overall assessment; treatment satisfaction and safety information will also be collected.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants with an effective overall assessment at Week 24
title: Observational Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of Kremezin IDT/Fine Gran in Progressive Chronic Kidney Disease Patients.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to testing the perioperative inhaled hydrogen (H2) administration's effects during atrial fibrillation ablations (AF) to reduce both early and late recurrences associated with this procedure.

Researchers will compare H2 inhalation to the standard of care to see if we observe a reduction in AF recurrence after ablation but also a reduction in rehospitalizations or emergency visits for cardioversion, and consequently an improvement in quality of life.

Participants will:

* have an AF ablation associated to an hydrogen therapy or standard of care
* complete quality of life questionnaires
* record ECG on KardiaMobile©
* Keep a diary of their symptoms
* have a blood test
* have 2 follow-up visits (after 3 and 12 months) and 2 phone calls (after 6 and 9 months)
primary_outcomes: Effectiveness of inhaled hydrogen therapy on early recurrences of atrial fibrillation post-ablation and on the improvement of quality of life at 3 months
title: Inhaled Hydrogen Therapy's Effect on Early Recurrences of Atrial Fibrillation Post-ablation.

brief_summary:
The prevalence of dementia and diabetes has increased in recent decades. The WHO forecasts an increase in the all-cause dementia prevalence to 152 million by 2050. Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is a well-known risk factor for dementia. The prevalence of T2D was estimated to be 6.28% (462 million people) worldwide, and 22% among people aged 70 years and older. Even pre-diabetes has been shown to be a risk factor for all-cause dementia, Alzheimer¿s disease (AD) and vascular dementia (VD).

There are various mechanisms by which T2D and dementia are connected. First, there are atherosclerotic consequences of T2D that favour VD. T2D is strongly associated with micro- and macrovascular diseases. This association is essentially determined by diabetes duration. Oxidative stress is the direct result of the imbalance between the production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and intracellular antioxidant defences. It is involved in the onset of diabetes and neurological pathologies such as AD, Parkinson¿s disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Therefore, as oxidative stress is a common pathway in diabetes and dementia, the evaluation of oxidative stress, using specific and direct biomarkers, is necessary to monitor the risk of dementia in patients with diabetes. Furthermore, it is important to study the mechanisms that lead to changes in the oxidative state, in order to define new therapeutic targets that allow delaying the eventual onset of dementia.

This project aims at defining how 1) soluble (s)NOX2-derived peptide(dp), a new direct biomarker of oxidative stress, could be used to stratify the risk of dementia in T2D patients; 2) if p47phox, a key cytosolic subunit that drives NOX2 activation, could be considered a therapeutic target to reduce oxidative stress-mediated dementia in T2D.

A clinical Aim will collect data of a T2D population to evaluate cognitive function, by the Multidimensional geriatric assessment (MGA) and cognitive biomarkers such as brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and ß-amyloid 42/40 and oxidative stress by sNOX2dp.

A second Aim will explore the contribution of NOX2 activation in the thrombotic process and cognitive impairment in T2D patients by the evaluation of endothelial dysfunction, as a thrombogenic risk factor, and quantitative analysis of the thrombus formation process.

Finally, a preclinical Aim will test the hypothesis that p47phox could be a therapeutic target to prevent oxidative stress-mediated dementia in T2D. Specifically, we tested the effects of the p47phox inhibitor peptide both in vitro, in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC), and in animal models (C57BL/6J) of high-fat diet (HFD)-induced diabetes.

Considering the prevalence of dementia in T2D and the uncertainty in their management, the proposed work is expected to generate results of immediate clinical significance.
primary_outcomes: Multidimensional geriatric assessment (MGA): MMSE
Multidimensional geriatric assessment (MGA): MoCA
Multidimensional geriatric assessment (MGA): SPMSQ
Multidimensional geriatric assessment (MGA): SBT
Lifestyle habits: nutritional assessment
Lifestyle habits: daily activity
Cognitive function evaluation: biomarker BDNF
Cognitive function evaluation: biomarker ß-amyloid 42/40
NOX2-mediated oxidative stress
title: Cardiovascular And Dementia Risk in diabeTes: the Role of Nox2- Related Oxidative Stress.

brief_summary: In order to promote healthy ageing and independent living, the World Health Organization recommends older adults to engage in resistance exercise at least twice weekly. However, only a minority of the older population complies with these guidelines, stressing the urgent need to develop comprehensive strategies to implement resistance exercise programs in the community. This PhD project will be performed in close collaboration with IPitup vzw, who developed outdoor activity benches, an accommodating smartphone app with exercise instructions and training courses as a low-cost modality for resistance exercise in the general population. The aim is to build upon these existing structures and develop an optimized, progressive resistance exercise program for community-dwelling older adults, which can be performed in small groups without the need for specialized training experts. The program's feasibility, defined in terms of safety, adherence, usability and acceptability, will be tested.
interventions: 6-week outdoor strength training program using activity benches and a smartphone application
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants Experiencing Adverse Events
Participant Adherence Rate
System Usability Scale (SUS)
Net Promoter Score (NPS)
Participant Acceptability of the Intervention
Completion Rate of Data Collection Procedures
Change in Lower Limb Muscle Strength and Power
Implementation Barriers and Facilitators Identified During Focus Groups
title: Feasibility Study of an Outdoor Strength Training Program for Older Adults

brief_summary:
A prospective, multicenter, non-interventional, observational cohort study on the use of a pharmacological agent, conducted within Infectious Diseases units-and, where available, as part of multidisciplinary teams for infective endocarditis-selected according to predefined feasibility criteria. Enrollment will be consecutive and will include all eligible patients for whom fosfomycin has already been initiated, or is initiated by the treating clinician, as part of routine clinical practice.

The decision to prescribe fosfomycin, the dosage, antibiotic combinations, duration of treatment, diagnostic tests, and any potential cardiac surgery strategy will remain entirely independent of the study and subject to local clinical judgment.

The study population will consist of adult patients with a diagnosis of definite or probable infective endocarditis, according to the 2023 Duke-ISCVID criteria, who have received at least one dose of intravenous (IV) fosfomycin as part of the antibiotic regimen for the clinical episode under observation. The availability of the minimum set of clinical, therapeutic, and microbiological data required by the protocol is a necessary requirement for inclusion.

Primary objective To describe the overall clinical outcomes and safety profile of fosfomycin-containing antibiotic regimens used in clinical practice for the treatment of infective endocarditis, assessed by the proportion of overall therapeutic success at a predefined 90-day follow-up and the incidence of adverse events of interest.

Secondary objectives To describe the methods of fosfomycin use in this setting, including clinical indication, timing of initiation, dosage, duration, combination agents, and the rationale behind the therapeutic choice.

To describe the clinical, microbiological, echocardiographic, and imaging characteristics of the enrolled patients.

To evaluate early and late microbiological outcomes, including blood culture clearance, persistence of bacteremia, microbiological recurrence, emergence of resistance, and relapse.

To describe the safety profile of fosfomycin, with particular attention to sodium overload, hypokalemia, electrolyte imbalances, renal toxicity, and adverse events leading to modification or discontinuation of treatment.

To explore the association between patterns of fosfomycin use and clinical or microbiological outcomes, without the intent of establishing causal inference.

To describe microbiological data related to fosfomycin in a standardized manner, specifying the raw MIC value, the antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) method, the interpretive criteria applied, and whether or not categorization according to applicable clinical breakpoints is possible.
primary_outcomes: To describe the overall clinical outcomes and safety profile of fosfomycin-containing antibiotic regimens used for the treatment of infective endocarditis, assessed by the proportion of overall therapeutic success at a predefined 90-days follow up+safety
title: Study of Fosfomycin-containing Antibiotic Regimens for the Treatment of Infective Endocarditis in Clinical Practice

brief_summary:
Heart failure is a chronic condition associated with reduced exercise capacity, physical inactivity, and impaired quality of life. Promoting regular physical activity is an important component of HF management; however, maintaining adequate physical activity levels remains challenging for many patients. Mobile health technologies may provide an effective approach to support physical activity through individualized monitoring, feedback, goal setting, and educational interventions.

The aim of this randomized controlled trial is to evaluate the effect of a mobile application on physical activity behavior in patients with HF.

This single-blind, two-arm randomized controlled trial will be conducted among patients with HF followed at the cardiology outpatient clinics of İzzet Baysal Education and Research Hospital, Bolu, Türkiye. Eligible participants will be randomly assigned to intervention and control groups in a 1:1 ratio.

Participants in the intervention group will use a mobile application integrated with smart wristbands for 12 weeks. The application will enable participants to monitor their physical activity duration and heart rate, set weekly and monthly exercise goals, receive visual feedback, and access educational videos and motivational messages. Before the home-based monitoring period, participants will attend supervised exercise sessions three times per week for one month under the supervision of an expert physiotherapist. These sessions will help determine individualized target heart rate levels, familiarize participants with the application and smart wristbands, and assess exercise tolerance.

Participants in the control group will receive standard care and individualized structured verbal education about the importance of physical activity, practical activity recommendations, and precautions to be considered before, during, and after exercise. They will not receive the technology-supported intervention.

The primary outcome will be the change in physical activity behavior, assessed using the Simple Physical Activity Questionnaire (SIMPAQ). Secondary outcomes will include health-related quality of life, assessed using the Left Ventricular Dysfunction Questionnaire (LVD-36). Physical activity and quality-of-life assessments will be conducted at baseline and during the follow-up period.

This study is expected to provide evidence regarding the potential contribution of mobile application-supported physical activity monitoring to promoting physical activity behavior and improving quality of life among individuals with HF.
primary_outcomes: Physical activity behavior
title: Mobile Application to Improve Physical Activity in Patients With Heart Failure

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to find out whether a reminiscence therapy-based social group work intervention (AT-GSH) improves psychological well-being, quality of life, and cognitive status in older adults living in long-term institutional care who are at risk of mild cognitive impairment.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does AT-GSH improve psychological well-being shortly after the intervention?
* Does AT-GSH improve psychological well-being at the 12-week follow-up?
* Does AT-GSH improve quality of life and cognitive status shortly after the intervention and at the 12-week follow-up?

The study plans to include 44 adults aged 60 years or older who meet the study's screening criteria. Participants will be randomly assigned to an intervention group or a wait-list control group.

Participants in the intervention group will attend a preparation meeting followed by eight weekly, 60-minute face-to-face sessions in closed groups of 6 to 10 members. The sessions will involve recalling, sharing, and reflecting on memories from different periods of life.

Researchers will compare this group with participants in the wait-list control group, who will continue receiving the institution's usual health, care, and social activity services.

Participants in the intervention group will complete assessments before the intervention, within 1 to 7 days after the final intervention session, and 12 weeks (plus or minus one week) after the final session. Participants in the wait-list control group will complete assessments during the same calendar weeks. The main comparison will focus on psychological well-being shortly after the intervention, taking initial psychological well-being scores into account.

After the final follow-up assessment, the wait-list control group will be offered the same intervention on a voluntary basis.
primary_outcomes: Psychological Well-Being Score at Post-Intervention
title: Reminiscence Therapy-Based Social Group Work for Older Adults in Long-Term Institutional Care

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate the use of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) to treat depression during pregnancy and the first year after childbirth. TMS is a noninvasive treatment that uses magnetic pulses applied to the scalp to stimulate areas of the brain involved in depression. The main goal of the study is to determine whether TMS treatment is feasible, acceptable, and safe for women with perinatal depression. The study will also collect preliminary information about whether TMS reduces symptoms of depression and whether improvements are maintained after treatment.

Up to 100 women age 22 years and older who have major depression and are either 12 to 28 weeks pregnant or within 12 months after giving birth will participate. All participants will receive TMS; there is no placebo or comparison group. Participants will receive 20 to 36 TMS treatment sessions over approximately 4 to 8 weeks, with up to five sessions per week. Depression and other mental health symptoms, treatment attendance, satisfaction with treatment, and safety will be assessed before, during, and approximately one month after TMS treatment.

The study hypothesis is that TMS will be a feasible and acceptable treatment for women with perinatal depression, as shown by participants completing and adhering to treatment, acceptable treatment satisfaction, and appropriate safety outcomes. The study will also explore whether depressive symptoms improve during TMS treatment and whether improvement is sustained one month after treatment. For women who participate while pregnant, the study team will review maternal and infant medical records approximately six months after delivery to assess pregnancy, delivery, postpartum, and infant health outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Retention Rate
title: Transcranial Magnetic Therapy (TMS) for Treatment of Perinatal Depression

brief_summary: MASLD and its inflammatory form, MASH, are major public health concerns due to their high prevalence and association with hepatic and cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Although extensively studied in type 2 diabetes (T2D), their pathophysiology in type 1 diabetes (T1D) remains poorly understood. Given the differences in immune mechanisms between T1D, primarily involving adaptive immunity, and T2D, associated with chronic innate immune activation, MASH may involve distinct immunoinflammatory pathways depending on the type of diabetes. This cross-sectional study aims to identify specific immunological and transcriptomic signatures associated with MASLD/MASH in patients with T1D and compare them with those observed in T2D, ultimately improving understanding of disease mechanisms and hepatic and cardiovascular risk stratification.
primary_outcomes: Comparison of circulating immune-cell subset frequencies according to liver status in patients with type 1 diabetes
Comparison of circulating immune-cell gene expression profiles according to liver status in patients with type 1 diabetes
title: Immunological Signatures of MASLD and MASH in Patients With Type 1 Diabetes
